anchor_verdict.rationale: The 12 top-level categories and their L1/L2 spine are coherent and complete: the natural / formal / applied / social / humanities / arts axis is standard, and the survival-through-post-disaster-rebuilding tail is a deliberate, internally consistent 'knowledge ark' design that should not be second-guessed. No top-level science is missing and no L1 is badly miscategorised. Two dual-classifications exist by design (Software Engineering under both CS 02.02.04 and Engineering 03.01.10; Logic under Formal Sciences 02.03 and Philosophy 05.02.05) but both are legitimate cross-listings, not defects, and re-baking the layout to merge them would cost more than it fixes. The physics asymmetry — 8 settled core fields sit empty while a Quantum-Gravity cluster is deeply built — is a CONTENT gap, not a spine flaw: the L2 branches themselves are named and placed correctly, they simply need L3/L4 populated. Bless the spine.

priority_domains.name: Thermodynamics
priority_domains.why_important: Settled foundational physics governing heat, energy and entropy; underpins every engine, chemical reaction, engineering process and the arrow of time. Completely empty.

priority_domains.name: Electromagnetism
priority_domains.why_important: One of the four fundamental interactions and the basis of all electrical technology, optics and modern electronics. A first-tier gap in any science reference.

priority_domains.name: Relativity
priority_domains.why_important: Einstein's theories of space, time and gravity; the framework behind GPS, cosmology and black-hole physics. Foundational and fully settled, yet absent.

priority_domains.name: Nuclear Physics
priority_domains.why_important: The physics of the nucleus — binding energy, radioactivity, fission and fusion — powering reactors, medicine, dating methods and stellar energy. Empty.

priority_domains.name: Particle Physics
priority_domains.why_important: The Standard Model of matter and its interactions, the deepest settled account of what the universe is made of. A cornerstone gap.

priority_domains.name: Astrophysics
priority_domains.why_important: The physics of stars, compact objects and the interstellar medium — how the universe makes and destroys structure. High importance, empty.

priority_domains.name: Geophysics
priority_domains.why_important: The physics of the Earth — seismology, geomagnetism, geodynamics — foundational to hazard science and planetary understanding. Empty but narrower than the core fields.

priority_domains.name: Biophysics
priority_domains.why_important: Physical principles applied to living systems, bridging physics and biology. Important and empty, but a hybrid field better kept lighter than the pure core.

pillars.name: Laws of Thermodynamics
pillars.description_en: The four foundational laws that govern energy, heat and entropy in every physical system, from the zeroth law defining temperature to the third law's absolute-zero limit.
pillars.description_cs: Čtyři základní zákony, jimiž se řídí energie, teplo a entropie v každém fyzikálním systému — od nultého zákona definujícího teplotu po třetí zákon a mez absolutní nuly.

pillars.name: Thermodynamic Potentials & Relations
pillars.description_en: The state functions — internal energy, enthalpy, Helmholtz and Gibbs free energy — and the Maxwell relations and Legendre transforms that connect them.
pillars.description_cs: Stavové funkce — vnitřní energie, entalpie, Helmholtzova a Gibbsova volná energie — a Maxwellovy relace a Legendreovy transformace, které je propojují.

pillars.name: Heat Engines & Cycles
pillars.description_en: How cyclic processes convert heat into work, the efficiency limits imposed by the second law, and the idealised cycles that model real engines and refrigerators.
pillars.description_cs: Jak cyklické děje přeměňují teplo na práci, meze účinnosti dané druhým zákonem a idealizované cykly modelující reálné motory a chladicí zařízení.

pillars.name: Phase Transitions & Equilibria
pillars.description_en: Changes of state and coexistence of phases: phase diagrams, latent heat, the Clausius-Clapeyron relation, and the classification and criticality of transitions.
pillars.description_cs: Změny skupenství a koexistence fází: fázové diagramy, latentní teplo, Clausiova–Clapeyronova rovnice a klasifikace a kritičnost přechodů.

pillars.name: Statistical Mechanics
pillars.description_en: The microscopic foundation of thermodynamics: how the statistics of many particles gives rise to macroscopic laws through ensembles, the partition function and entropy as counting.
pillars.description_cs: Mikroskopický základ termodynamiky: jak statistika mnoha částic vede k makroskopickým zákonům pomocí souborů, partiční funkce a entropie jako počítání stavů.

pillars.name: Kinetic Theory & Transport
pillars.description_en: The dynamics of molecular motion and how it carries mass, momentum and energy: the kinetic theory of gases and the transport processes of diffusion, viscosity and conduction.
pillars.description_cs: Dynamika molekulárního pohybu a jak přenáší hmotu, hybnost a energii: kinetická teorie plynů a transportní děje difuze, viskozity a vedení tepla.

pillars.name: Electrostatics
pillars.description_en: The physics of stationary electric charge: Coulomb's law, the electric field and potential, Gauss's law, and the behaviour of conductors and capacitors.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzika nehybného elektrického náboje: Coulombův zákon, elektrické pole a potenciál, Gaussův zákon a chování vodičů a kondenzátorů.

pillars.name: Magnetostatics
pillars.description_en: The physics of steady currents and their magnetic fields: the Biot-Savart and Ampère laws, magnetic force, and the magnetic properties of matter.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzika ustálených proudů a jejich magnetických polí: Biotův–Savartův a Ampérův zákon, magnetická síla a magnetické vlastnosti látek.

pillars.name: Electrodynamics
pillars.description_en: Time-varying fields and their unification: electromagnetic induction, the displacement current, and Maxwell's equations as the complete classical field theory.
pillars.description_cs: Časově proměnná pole a jejich sjednocení: elektromagnetická indukce, posuvný proud a Maxwellovy rovnice jako úplná klasická teorie pole.

pillars.name: Electromagnetic Waves & Optics
pillars.description_en: The propagation of electromagnetic fields as waves: the electromagnetic spectrum, energy and momentum transport, and the optics of reflection, refraction and interference.
pillars.description_cs: Šíření elektromagnetického pole ve formě vln: elektromagnetické spektrum, přenos energie a hybnosti a optika odrazu, lomu a interference.

pillars.name: Electromagnetism in Matter
pillars.description_en: How materials respond to fields: polarization and dielectrics, magnetization and magnetic materials, conduction, and the resulting macroscopic field equations.
pillars.description_cs: Jak látky reagují na pole: polarizace a dielektrika, magnetizace a magnetické materiály, vedení proudu a výsledné makroskopické rovnice pole.

pillars.name: Circuits & Electromagnetic Technology
pillars.description_en: The engineering physics of circuits and devices: Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws, alternating current, and the electromagnetic principles behind motors, generators and antennas.
pillars.description_cs: Technická fyzika obvodů a zařízení: Ohmův a Kirchhoffovy zákony, střídavý proud a elektromagnetické principy motorů, generátorů a antén.

pillars.name: Special Relativity
pillars.description_en: Einstein's 1905 theory of space and time in inertial frames: the constancy of the speed of light, the relativity of simultaneity, time dilation and length contraction, and the Lorentz transformation.
pillars.description_cs: Einsteinova teorie prostoru a času z roku 1905 v inerciálních soustavách: stálost rychlosti světla, relativita současnosti, dilatace času a kontrakce délek a Lorentzova transformace.

pillars.name: Relativistic Dynamics
pillars.description_en: Mechanics at high speed: relativistic momentum and energy, the mass-energy equivalence, four-vectors, and the union of space and time into Minkowski spacetime.
pillars.description_cs: Mechanika při vysokých rychlostech: relativistická hybnost a energie, ekvivalence hmoty a energie, čtyřvektory a sjednocení prostoru a času do Minkowského časoprostoru.

pillars.name: General Relativity
pillars.description_en: Einstein's geometric theory of gravity: the equivalence principle, curved spacetime, geodesic motion, and the field equations relating curvature to energy and momentum.
pillars.description_cs: Einsteinova geometrická teorie gravitace: princip ekvivalence, zakřivený časoprostor, pohyb po geodetikách a rovnice pole spojující křivost s energií a hybností.

pillars.name: Gravitation & Spacetime Solutions
pillars.description_en: Solutions of the field equations and their physics: black holes, gravitational waves, and the exact geometries that describe stars, collapsed objects and the expanding universe.
pillars.description_cs: Řešení rovnic pole a jejich fyzika: černé díry, gravitační vlny a přesné geometrie popisující hvězdy, zhroucené objekty a rozpínající se vesmír.

pillars.name: Tests & Applications of Relativity
pillars.description_en: The experimental confirmation and practical use of relativity, from Mercury's perihelion and light bending to gravitational-wave detection and the relativistic corrections in satellite navigation.
pillars.description_cs: Experimentální potvrzení a praktické využití relativity, od stáčení perihelia Merkuru a ohybu světla po detekci gravitačních vln a relativistické korekce v družicové navigaci.

pillars.name: Nuclear Structure
pillars.description_en: The composition and organisation of the atomic nucleus: protons and neutrons, binding energy, nuclear size and shape, and the models that explain nuclear stability.
pillars.description_cs: Složení a uspořádání atomového jádra: protony a neutrony, vazebná energie, velikost a tvar jádra a modely vysvětlující jadernou stabilitu.

pillars.name: Radioactivity & Decay
pillars.description_en: The spontaneous transformation of unstable nuclei: alpha, beta and gamma decay, decay laws and half-lives, decay chains, and the applications of radioactive dating and tracing.
pillars.description_cs: Samovolná přeměna nestabilních jader: alfa, beta a gama rozpad, zákony rozpadu a poločasy, rozpadové řady a využití radioaktivního datování a značkování.

pillars.name: Nuclear Reactions
pillars.description_en: Induced transformations of nuclei: reaction kinematics and cross sections, conservation laws, and the mechanisms of scattering, capture and transmutation.
pillars.description_cs: Vynucené přeměny jader: kinematika reakcí a účinné průřezy, zákony zachování a mechanismy rozptylu, záchytu a transmutace.

pillars.name: Fission, Fusion & Energy
pillars.description_en: The two routes to nuclear energy: the splitting of heavy nuclei and the merging of light ones, the physics of chain reactions and confinement, and their use in reactors and weapons.
pillars.description_cs: Dvě cesty k jaderné energii: štěpení těžkých jader a slučování lehkých, fyzika řetězových reakcí a udržení a jejich využití v reaktorech a zbraních.

pillars.name: Applied & Astrophysical Nuclear Physics
pillars.description_en: Nuclear physics in practice and in the cosmos: nuclear medicine and radiation detection, radiation protection, and the nucleosynthesis that forges the elements in stars.
pillars.description_cs: Jaderná fyzika v praxi a ve vesmíru: nukleární medicína a detekce záření, radiační ochrana a nukleosyntéza, která ve hvězdách vytváří prvky.

pillars.name: The Standard Model
pillars.description_en: The theory of elementary particles and their interactions: the quarks and leptons of matter, the gauge bosons carrying forces, and the Higgs boson that gives them mass.
pillars.description_cs: Teorie elementárních částic a jejich interakcí: kvarky a leptony tvořící hmotu, kalibrační bosony přenášející síly a Higgsův boson, který jim dodává hmotnost.

pillars.name: Fundamental Interactions
pillars.description_en: The forces between particles as gauge field theories: quantum electrodynamics, the strong interaction and quantum chromodynamics, and the weak interaction with electroweak unification.
pillars.description_cs: Síly mezi částicemi jako kalibrační teorie pole: kvantová elektrodynamika, silná interakce a kvantová chromodynamika a slabá interakce s elektroslabým sjednocením.

pillars.name: Symmetries & Conservation Laws
pillars.description_en: The symmetry principles organising particle physics: conservation laws from continuous symmetries, the discrete symmetries C, P and T, and the spontaneous symmetry breaking behind mass generation.
pillars.description_cs: Principy symetrie uspořádávající částicovou fyziku: zákony zachování ze spojitých symetrií, diskrétní symetrie C, P a T a spontánní narušení symetrie za vznikem hmotnosti.

pillars.name: Experimental Particle Physics
pillars.description_en: How particles are produced and observed: accelerators and colliders, detector technologies, and the statistical analysis by which discoveries are established.
pillars.description_cs: Jak se částice vytvářejí a pozorují: urychlovače a srážeče, detekční technologie a statistická analýza, kterou se prokazují objevy.

pillars.name: Beyond the Standard Model
pillars.description_en: The open questions and proposed extensions: neutrino mass and oscillation, the identity of dark matter, supersymmetry and grand unification, and the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe.
pillars.description_cs: Otevřené otázky a navrhovaná rozšíření: hmotnost a oscilace neutrin, povaha temné hmoty, supersymetrie a velké sjednocení a asymetrie hmoty a antihmoty ve vesmíru.

pillars.name: Stellar Structure & Evolution
pillars.description_en: The physics of stars: hydrostatic and thermal balance, energy generation by fusion, the main sequence, and the evolution of stars from birth to their final states.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzika hvězd: hydrostatická a tepelná rovnováha, uvolňování energie fúzí, hlavní posloupnost a vývoj hvězd od zrození po jejich konečné stavy.

pillars.name: Compact Objects
pillars.description_en: The dense remnants of stellar death: white dwarfs, neutron stars and stellar black holes, supported against gravity by degeneracy pressure or not at all.
pillars.description_cs: Husté pozůstatky zániku hvězd: bílí trpaslíci, neutronové hvězdy a hvězdné černé díry, držené proti gravitaci degeneračním tlakem, nebo vůbec ne.

pillars.name: Interstellar Medium & Star Formation
pillars.description_en: The gas and dust between the stars and the collapse that turns it into new stars: molecular clouds, gravitational instability, and the physics of accretion and protostars.
pillars.description_cs: Plyn a prach mezi hvězdami a kolaps, který jej mění v nové hvězdy: molekulární mračna, gravitační nestabilita a fyzika akrece a protohvězd.

pillars.name: Galactic & Extragalactic Astrophysics
pillars.description_en: The structure and dynamics of galaxies and the largest systems: galactic rotation and dark matter, active galactic nuclei, and clusters and the cosmic web.
pillars.description_cs: Struktura a dynamika galaxií a největších soustav: rotace galaxií a temná hmota, aktivní galaktická jádra a kupy galaxií a kosmická síť.

pillars.name: High-Energy & Multi-Messenger Astrophysics
pillars.description_en: The most violent phenomena and the many channels that reveal them: supernovae and their remnants, cosmic rays, gamma-ray bursts, and observation through light, particles and gravitational waves.
pillars.description_cs: Nejprudší jevy a mnoho kanálů, jimiž se projevují: supernovy a jejich pozůstatky, kosmické záření, záblesky gama a pozorování světlem, částicemi a gravitačními vlnami.

pillars.name: Seismology & Earth's Interior
pillars.description_en: The study of seismic waves and what they reveal about the planet's layered structure: earthquake sources, wave propagation, and the crust, mantle and core.
pillars.description_cs: Studium seismických vln a toho, co odhalují o vrstevnaté stavbě planety: zdroje zemětřesení, šíření vln a kůra, plášť a jádro.

pillars.name: Geomagnetism & the Geodynamo
pillars.description_en: The Earth's magnetic field, its generation by convection in the liquid outer core, its variations and reversals, and the record it leaves in rocks.
pillars.description_cs: Magnetické pole Země, jeho vznik konvekcí v tekutém vnějším jádru, jeho proměny a přepólování a záznam, který zanechává v horninách.

pillars.name: Gravity, Geodesy & Earth's Shape
pillars.description_en: The Earth's gravity field and figure: geodesy and reference surfaces, gravity anomalies, isostasy, and the measurement of the planet's shape and rotation.
pillars.description_cs: Tíhové pole a tvar Země: geodézie a referenční plochy, tíhové anomálie, izostáze a měření tvaru a rotace planety.

pillars.name: Geodynamics & Plate Tectonics
pillars.description_en: The physics driving the solid Earth's motion: mantle convection, plate tectonics, and the heat flow and deformation that shape the surface.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzika pohánějící pohyb pevné Země: konvekce v plášti, desková tektonika a tepelný tok a deformace, jež utvářejí povrch.

pillars.name: Molecular Biophysics
pillars.description_en: The physics of biological macromolecules: protein structure and folding, molecular motors, and the forces and energetics that govern molecular machines.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzika biologických makromolekul: struktura a sbalování bílkovin, molekulární motory a síly a energetika řídící molekulární stroje.

pillars.name: Membrane & Neural Biophysics
pillars.description_en: The physics of cell membranes and excitable cells: ion transport and membrane potentials, the action potential, and the electrical signalling of nerves.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzika buněčných membrán a dráždivých buněk: transport iontů a membránové potenciály, akční potenciál a elektrická signalizace nervů.

pillars.name: Biomechanics
pillars.description_en: The mechanics of living matter: the material properties of tissues, the forces in movement and locomotion, and fluid flow in circulation and respiration.
pillars.description_cs: Mechanika živé hmoty: materiálové vlastnosti tkání, síly při pohybu a lokomoci a proudění tekutin v oběhu a dýchání.

pillars.name: Biophysical Techniques
pillars.description_en: The physical methods that image and probe living systems: structural determination, single-molecule and optical techniques, and the physics of medical imaging.
pillars.description_cs: Fyzikální metody zobrazující a zkoumající živé systémy: určování struktury, jednomolekulové a optické techniky a fyzika lékařského zobrazování.

new_blocks.name: Zeroth Law & Temperature
new_blocks.description_en: Defines thermal equilibrium and temperature: if two systems are each in equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other, making temperature a consistent, transitive property.
new_blocks.description_cs: Definuje tepelnou rovnováhu a teplotu: jsou-li dva systémy v rovnováze se třetím, jsou v rovnováze i navzájem, což činí z teploty konzistentní, tranzitivní veličinu.

brief_concepts.name: Thermal equilibrium
brief_concepts.definition: State in which no net heat flows between systems in contact, so their temperatures are equal.

brief_concepts.name: Temperature scales
brief_concepts.definition: Empirical (Celsius, Fahrenheit) and absolute (Kelvin) scales measuring the degree of thermal agitation.

brief_concepts.name: Thermometry
brief_concepts.definition: Measurement of temperature via a property that varies reproducibly with it, such as gas volume or resistance.

brief_concepts.name: Transitivity of equilibrium
brief_concepts.definition: The logical basis of the zeroth law that lets temperature label equivalence classes of systems.

new_blocks.name: First Law & Internal Energy
new_blocks.description_en: Energy conservation for thermodynamic systems: the change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done, so heat and work are two forms of the same conserved quantity.
new_blocks.description_cs: Zachování energie pro termodynamické systémy: změna vnitřní energie se rovná dodanému teplu zmenšenému o vykonanou práci, takže teplo a práce jsou dvě formy téže zachovávané veličiny.

brief_concepts.name: Internal energy
brief_concepts.definition: The total microscopic kinetic and potential energy of a system, a state function.

brief_concepts.name: Heat and work
brief_concepts.definition: The two path-dependent ways energy crosses a system boundary.

brief_concepts.name: Work of expansion
brief_concepts.definition: Pressure-volume work done by or on a gas as its volume changes.

brief_concepts.name: Enthalpy
brief_concepts.definition: The combination U + pV, convenient for processes at constant pressure.

brief_concepts.name: Heat capacity
brief_concepts.definition: The heat required to raise a system's temperature by one degree, at constant volume or pressure.

new_blocks.name: Second Law & Entropy
new_blocks.description_en: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases, setting the direction of spontaneous change and the irreversibility of natural processes; it forbids perfect conversion of heat into work.
new_blocks.description_cs: Entropie izolovaného systému nikdy neklesá, což určuje směr samovolných dějů a nevratnost přírodních procesů; zakazuje dokonalou přeměnu tepla na práci.

brief_concepts.name: Entropy
brief_concepts.definition: A state function measuring the dispersal of energy and the number of accessible microstates.

brief_concepts.name: Clausius statement
brief_concepts.definition: Heat does not spontaneously flow from a colder to a hotter body.

brief_concepts.name: Kelvin-Planck statement
brief_concepts.definition: No cyclic process can convert heat entirely into work with no other effect.

brief_concepts.name: Reversible vs irreversible
brief_concepts.definition: Idealised quasi-static processes conserve total entropy; real processes generate it.

brief_concepts.name: Arrow of time
brief_concepts.definition: The thermodynamic asymmetry that distinguishes past from future via increasing entropy.

new_blocks.name: Third Law & Absolute Zero
new_blocks.description_en: As temperature approaches absolute zero the entropy of a perfect crystal approaches a constant minimum, implying absolute zero is unattainable in finitely many steps.
new_blocks.description_cs: Když se teplota blíží absolutní nule, entropie dokonalého krystalu se blíží konstantnímu minimu, z čehož plyne, že absolutní nuly nelze dosáhnout konečným počtem kroků.

brief_concepts.name: Nernst heat theorem
brief_concepts.definition: Entropy change of a reaction approaches zero as temperature approaches absolute zero.

brief_concepts.name: Residual entropy
brief_concepts.definition: Nonzero ground-state entropy in disordered solids such as glasses or ice.

brief_concepts.name: Unattainability
brief_concepts.definition: No finite sequence of processes can cool a system to exactly absolute zero.

brief_concepts.name: Cryogenics
brief_concepts.definition: The production and study of very low temperatures approaching the absolute-zero limit.

new_blocks.name: Free Energies
new_blocks.description_en: Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies combine energy and entropy into potentials whose minima locate equilibrium at constant temperature-volume or temperature-pressure, and whose changes bound available work.
new_blocks.description_cs: Helmholtzova a Gibbsova volná energie spojují energii a entropii do potenciálů, jejichž minima určují rovnováhu při konstantní teplotě a objemu či teplotě a tlaku a jejichž změny omezují využitelnou práci.

brief_concepts.name: Helmholtz free energy
brief_concepts.definition: F = U - TS, minimised at equilibrium at constant temperature and volume.

brief_concepts.name: Gibbs free energy
brief_concepts.definition: G = H - TS, minimised at equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure.

brief_concepts.name: Spontaneity criterion
brief_concepts.definition: A process is spontaneous when the relevant free energy decreases.

brief_concepts.name: Chemical potential
brief_concepts.definition: The change in free energy when one particle is added, driving mass transfer and reaction.

brief_concepts.name: Maximum work
brief_concepts.definition: The free-energy change sets the greatest useful work extractable from a process.

new_blocks.name: Maxwell Relations & State Functions
new_blocks.description_en: Equality of mixed second derivatives of the thermodynamic potentials yields the Maxwell relations, linking hard-to-measure quantities such as entropy changes to measurable pressure, volume and temperature data.
new_blocks.description_cs: Rovnost smíšených druhých derivací termodynamických potenciálů dává Maxwellovy relace, které spojují obtížně měřitelné veličiny, jako jsou změny entropie, s měřitelnými daty o tlaku, objemu a teplotě.

brief_concepts.name: State function
brief_concepts.definition: A quantity determined by the current state, independent of the path taken to reach it.

brief_concepts.name: Exact differential
brief_concepts.definition: The mathematical property of state functions ensuring path-independent changes.

brief_concepts.name: Legendre transform
brief_concepts.definition: The operation generating one potential from another by swapping conjugate variables.

brief_concepts.name: Conjugate variables
brief_concepts.definition: Paired quantities such as pressure-volume and temperature-entropy whose product is energy.

brief_concepts.name: Response functions
brief_concepts.definition: Measurable derivatives such as compressibility and thermal expansion linked by the relations.

new_blocks.name: Carnot Cycle & Efficiency
new_blocks.description_en: The Carnot cycle of two isothermal and two adiabatic steps is the most efficient possible heat engine between two reservoirs, its efficiency fixed by their temperatures alone and independent of the working substance.
new_blocks.description_cs: Carnotův cyklus ze dvou izotermických a dvou adiabatických dějů je nejúčinnějším možným tepelným strojem mezi dvěma zásobníky; jeho účinnost je dána pouze jejich teplotami a nezávisí na pracovní látce.

brief_concepts.name: Carnot efficiency
brief_concepts.definition: The maximum efficiency 1 - T_cold/T_hot achievable between two heat reservoirs.

brief_concepts.name: Reversible cycle
brief_concepts.definition: An idealised cycle run infinitely slowly so total entropy is conserved.

brief_concepts.name: Isothermal process
brief_concepts.definition: A step at constant temperature during which heat is exchanged with a reservoir.

brief_concepts.name: Adiabatic process
brief_concepts.definition: A step with no heat exchange, so all energy change is mechanical work.

brief_concepts.name: Carnot's theorem
brief_concepts.definition: No engine between two reservoirs can exceed the efficiency of a reversible one.

new_blocks.name: Practical Engine & Refrigeration Cycles
new_blocks.description_en: Real engines and refrigerators approximate idealised cycles — Otto, Diesel, Brayton, Rankine and the reversed vapour-compression cycle — each trading efficiency, power and practicality for a given application.
new_blocks.description_cs: Reálné motory a chladicí zařízení aproximují idealizované cykly — Ottův, Dieselův, Braytonův, Rankinův a obrácený kompresní chladicí cyklus — z nichž každý pro danou aplikaci volí kompromis mezi účinností, výkonem a praktičností.

brief_concepts.name: Otto cycle
brief_concepts.definition: The idealised cycle of a spark-ignition petrol engine.

brief_concepts.name: Diesel cycle
brief_concepts.definition: The compression-ignition cycle with heat added at constant pressure.

brief_concepts.name: Rankine cycle
brief_concepts.definition: The steam power cycle used in most thermal and nuclear power stations.

brief_concepts.name: Brayton cycle
brief_concepts.definition: The gas-turbine and jet-engine cycle of continuous compression, combustion and expansion.

brief_concepts.name: Refrigeration cycle
brief_concepts.definition: A reversed cycle that moves heat from cold to hot using input work.

brief_concepts.name: Coefficient of performance
brief_concepts.definition: The ratio of useful heating or cooling to the work input of a heat pump.

new_blocks.name: Phase Diagrams & Coexistence
new_blocks.description_en: Phase diagrams map which state of matter is stable at each pressure and temperature, with coexistence lines where phases meet, a triple point where three coexist, and a critical point where liquid and gas become indistinguishable.
new_blocks.description_cs: Fázové diagramy znázorňují, které skupenství je stabilní při daném tlaku a teplotě, s koexistenčními křivkami, kde se fáze setkávají, trojným bodem, kde koexistují tři fáze, a kritickým bodem, kde se kapalina a plyn stávají nerozlišitelnými.

brief_concepts.name: Triple point
brief_concepts.definition: The unique pressure and temperature at which solid, liquid and gas coexist.

brief_concepts.name: Critical point
brief_concepts.definition: The endpoint of the liquid-gas line beyond which the two phases merge.

brief_concepts.name: Clausius-Clapeyron relation
brief_concepts.definition: The equation giving the slope of a coexistence line from latent heat and volume change.

brief_concepts.name: Latent heat
brief_concepts.definition: The heat absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature.

brief_concepts.name: Gibbs phase rule
brief_concepts.definition: The relation fixing the number of independent variables among coexisting phases.

new_blocks.name: Critical Phenomena & Order Parameters
new_blocks.description_en: Near a continuous phase transition, fluctuations grow to all scales and thermodynamic quantities follow universal power laws set by critical exponents, independent of microscopic detail — the domain of universality classes.
new_blocks.description_cs: V blízkosti spojitého fázového přechodu narůstají fluktuace na všech škálách a termodynamické veličiny se řídí univerzálními mocninnými zákony určenými kritickými exponenty, nezávislými na mikroskopických detailech — jde o oblast tříd univerzality.

brief_concepts.name: Order parameter
brief_concepts.definition: A quantity that is zero in one phase and nonzero in the other, marking the transition.

brief_concepts.name: Critical exponents
brief_concepts.definition: The universal powers describing how quantities diverge or vanish near the critical point.

brief_concepts.name: Universality
brief_concepts.definition: The independence of critical behaviour from microscopic details, set by symmetry and dimension.

brief_concepts.name: First- vs second-order
brief_concepts.definition: Transitions with a latent heat and jump versus continuous ones with diverging susceptibility.

brief_concepts.name: Correlation length
brief_concepts.definition: The distance over which fluctuations are correlated, diverging at the critical point.

new_blocks.name: Statistical Ensembles
new_blocks.description_en: Statistical mechanics computes macroscopic properties by averaging over ensembles of microstates — microcanonical at fixed energy, canonical at fixed temperature, grand canonical at fixed chemical potential — that reproduce thermodynamics.
new_blocks.description_cs: Statistická mechanika počítá makroskopické vlastnosti průměrováním přes soubory mikrostavů — mikrokanonický při dané energii, kanonický při dané teplotě, velký kanonický při daném chemickém potenciálu — které reprodukují termodynamiku.

brief_concepts.name: Microstate
brief_concepts.definition: A complete specification of the positions and momenta of all particles.

brief_concepts.name: Microcanonical ensemble
brief_concepts.definition: The set of microstates at fixed energy, volume and particle number.

brief_concepts.name: Canonical ensemble
brief_concepts.definition: The distribution of a system in thermal contact with a heat bath at fixed temperature.

brief_concepts.name: Grand canonical ensemble
brief_concepts.definition: The distribution allowing exchange of both energy and particles with a reservoir.

brief_concepts.name: Boltzmann distribution
brief_concepts.definition: The probability of a microstate falling off exponentially with its energy over kT.

new_blocks.name: Partition Function & Entropy
new_blocks.description_en: The partition function sums Boltzmann factors over all microstates and is the generating function from which every thermodynamic quantity follows; Boltzmann's entropy S = k ln W ties entropy to the count of accessible microstates.
new_blocks.description_cs: Partiční funkce sčítá Boltzmannovy faktory přes všechny mikrostavy a je vytvořující funkcí, z níž plyne každá termodynamická veličina; Boltzmannova entropie S = k ln W spojuje entropii s počtem dostupných mikrostavů.

brief_concepts.name: Partition function
brief_concepts.definition: The sum over states weighting each by its Boltzmann factor, encoding all thermodynamics.

brief_concepts.name: Boltzmann entropy
brief_concepts.definition: Entropy as the logarithm of the number of microstates times Boltzmann's constant.

brief_concepts.name: Free energy from Z
brief_concepts.definition: The Helmholtz free energy given directly by minus kT times the log of the partition function.

brief_concepts.name: Equipartition theorem
brief_concepts.definition: Each quadratic degree of freedom carries an average energy of one half kT.

brief_concepts.name: Fluctuations
brief_concepts.definition: Statistical variations of energy and particle number, related to heat capacity and compressibility.

new_blocks.name: Quantum Statistics
new_blocks.description_en: Indistinguishable quantum particles obey Fermi-Dirac or Bose-Einstein statistics, explaining electron degeneracy in metals and stars, blackbody radiation, and Bose-Einstein condensation, with classical statistics as the dilute limit.
new_blocks.description_cs: Nerozlišitelné kvantové částice se řídí Fermiho–Diracovou nebo Boseho–Einsteinovou statistikou, což vysvětluje degeneraci elektronů v kovech a hvězdách, záření černého tělesa a Boseho–Einsteinovu kondenzaci, přičemž klasická statistika je jejich zředěnou limitou.

brief_concepts.name: Fermi-Dirac statistics
brief_concepts.definition: The distribution of fermions obeying the Pauli exclusion principle.

brief_concepts.name: Bose-Einstein statistics
brief_concepts.definition: The distribution of bosons, which can occupy the same state without limit.

brief_concepts.name: Degeneracy pressure
brief_concepts.definition: The pressure from the exclusion principle supporting white dwarfs and neutron stars.

brief_concepts.name: Blackbody radiation
brief_concepts.definition: The thermal photon spectrum explained by quantising electromagnetic modes.

brief_concepts.name: Bose-Einstein condensate
brief_concepts.definition: A macroscopic occupation of the ground state at very low temperature.

new_blocks.name: Kinetic Theory of Gases
new_blocks.description_en: Treating a gas as many colliding point particles derives pressure, temperature and the ideal-gas law from mechanics, and gives the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of molecular speeds and the mean free path between collisions.
new_blocks.description_cs: Pojetí plynu jako mnoha srážejících se hmotných bodů odvozuje tlak, teplotu a stavovou rovnici ideálního plynu z mechaniky a dává Maxwellovo–Boltzmannovo rozdělení rychlostí molekul a střední volnou dráhu mezi srážkami.

brief_concepts.name: Ideal gas law
brief_concepts.definition: The relation pV = NkT linking pressure, volume and temperature of a dilute gas.

brief_concepts.name: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution
brief_concepts.definition: The statistical distribution of molecular speeds in a gas at equilibrium.

brief_concepts.name: Mean free path
brief_concepts.definition: The average distance a molecule travels between successive collisions.

brief_concepts.name: Pressure from momentum
brief_concepts.definition: Gas pressure as the momentum transfer of molecules striking the walls.

brief_concepts.name: Real gas equations
brief_concepts.definition: Corrections such as the van der Waals equation accounting for molecular size and attraction.

new_blocks.name: Transport Processes
new_blocks.description_en: Gradients of concentration, velocity or temperature drive fluxes of matter, momentum and heat — diffusion, viscosity and thermal conduction — each described by a linear transport law and a molecular transport coefficient.
new_blocks.description_cs: Gradienty koncentrace, rychlosti nebo teploty vyvolávají toky látky, hybnosti a tepla — difuzi, viskozitu a vedení tepla — z nichž každý popisuje lineární transportní zákon a molekulární transportní koeficient.

brief_concepts.name: Diffusion
brief_concepts.definition: Net transport of particles down a concentration gradient, described by Fick's laws.

brief_concepts.name: Viscosity
brief_concepts.definition: The transport of momentum across a velocity gradient in a flowing fluid.

brief_concepts.name: Thermal conduction
brief_concepts.definition: The transport of heat down a temperature gradient, described by Fourier's law.

brief_concepts.name: Onsager reciprocity
brief_concepts.definition: Symmetry relations among coupled transport coefficients near equilibrium.

brief_concepts.name: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics
brief_concepts.definition: The framework describing entropy production in systems with steady fluxes.

new_blocks.name: Coulomb's Law & Electric Force
new_blocks.description_en: The force between point charges is proportional to their product and inversely proportional to the square of their separation, directed along the line joining them; this inverse-square law is the foundation of electrostatics.
new_blocks.description_cs: Síla mezi bodovými náboji je úměrná jejich součinu a nepřímo úměrná druhé mocnině jejich vzdálenosti a míří podél jejich spojnice; tento zákon převrácené druhé mocniny je základem elektrostatiky.

brief_concepts.name: Electric charge
brief_concepts.definition: The conserved property of matter that is the source of electromagnetic force, quantised in units of e.

brief_concepts.name: Coulomb's law
brief_concepts.definition: The inverse-square force law between two point charges.

brief_concepts.name: Superposition
brief_concepts.definition: The net force from many charges as the vector sum of individual Coulomb forces.

brief_concepts.name: Permittivity
brief_concepts.definition: The constant characterising how a medium reduces the electrostatic force within it.

new_blocks.name: Electric Field & Potential
new_blocks.description_en: The electric field assigns a force-per-charge vector to every point in space, and the electric potential its energy-per-charge; the field is the gradient of the potential, and field lines and equipotentials visualise both.
new_blocks.description_cs: Elektrické pole přiřazuje každému bodu prostoru vektor síly na jednotku náboje a elektrický potenciál energii na jednotku náboje; pole je gradientem potenciálu a siločáry a ekvipotenciály obojí znázorňují.

brief_concepts.name: Electric field
brief_concepts.definition: The force per unit charge experienced by a test charge at a point.

brief_concepts.name: Electric potential
brief_concepts.definition: The potential energy per unit charge, measured in volts.

brief_concepts.name: Field-potential relation
brief_concepts.definition: The field equals minus the spatial gradient of the potential.

brief_concepts.name: Dipole
brief_concepts.definition: A pair of equal and opposite charges whose field falls off faster than a single charge.

brief_concepts.name: Equipotential surface
brief_concepts.definition: A surface of constant potential, everywhere perpendicular to the field.

new_blocks.name: Gauss's Law
new_blocks.description_en: The electric flux through any closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by the permittivity; this restatement of the inverse-square law exploits symmetry to compute fields of charged spheres, lines and planes.
new_blocks.description_cs: Elektrický tok libovolnou uzavřenou plochou se rovná uzavřenému náboji dělenému permitivitou; toto přeformulování zákona převrácené druhé mocniny využívá symetrie k výpočtu polí nabitých koulí, přímek a rovin.

brief_concepts.name: Electric flux
brief_concepts.definition: The amount of electric field passing through a surface.

brief_concepts.name: Gauss's law
brief_concepts.definition: The relation between the flux through a closed surface and the charge it encloses.

brief_concepts.name: Gaussian surface
brief_concepts.definition: An imaginary closed surface chosen to exploit symmetry in field calculations.

brief_concepts.name: Divergence form
brief_concepts.definition: The differential statement that the field's divergence equals charge density over permittivity.

new_blocks.name: Conductors & Capacitance
new_blocks.description_en: In a conductor charge redistributes until the interior field vanishes and the surface is equipotential; capacitance measures the charge stored per unit voltage between conductors, storing energy in the electric field.
new_blocks.description_cs: Ve vodiči se náboj přerozdělí, dokud vnitřní pole nezmizí a povrch není ekvipotenciální; kapacita udává náboj uložený na jednotku napětí mezi vodiči a ukládá energii v elektrickém poli.

brief_concepts.name: Electrostatic shielding
brief_concepts.definition: The cancellation of interior fields by a conductor, the basis of the Faraday cage.

brief_concepts.name: Capacitance
brief_concepts.definition: The ratio of stored charge to the voltage between two conductors.

brief_concepts.name: Capacitor
brief_concepts.definition: A device of two conductors storing energy in the field between them.

brief_concepts.name: Field energy density
brief_concepts.definition: The energy stored per unit volume in an electric field, proportional to its square.

brief_concepts.name: Dielectric in a capacitor
brief_concepts.definition: An insulating filling that raises capacitance by reducing the internal field.

new_blocks.name: Magnetic Field & Force
new_blocks.description_en: Moving charges and currents create magnetic fields and feel forces in them: the Lorentz force acts perpendicular to both velocity and field, curving charged trajectories and driving the operation of motors.
new_blocks.description_cs: Pohybující se náboje a proudy vytvářejí magnetické pole a působí na ně v něm síla: Lorentzova síla míří kolmo k rychlosti i poli, zakřivuje dráhy nabitých částic a pohání motory.

brief_concepts.name: Lorentz force
brief_concepts.definition: The force qv×B on a charge moving through a magnetic field, plus the electric part.

brief_concepts.name: Magnetic field
brief_concepts.definition: The vector field produced by currents and felt by moving charges, denoted B.

brief_concepts.name: Cyclotron motion
brief_concepts.definition: The circular path of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field.

brief_concepts.name: Force on a current
brief_concepts.definition: The force on a current-carrying wire in a field, the basis of the electric motor.

brief_concepts.name: Magnetic dipole moment
brief_concepts.definition: The measure of a current loop's strength as a source of magnetic field.

new_blocks.name: Ampère's & Biot-Savart Laws
new_blocks.description_en: The Biot-Savart law gives the field of an arbitrary current element, while Ampère's law relates the field circulating around a loop to the enclosed current, providing a symmetry shortcut for fields of wires, solenoids and toroids.
new_blocks.description_cs: Biotův–Savartův zákon dává pole libovolného proudového elementu, zatímco Ampérův zákon spojuje pole cirkulující kolem smyčky s uzavřeným proudem a poskytuje symetrickou zkratku pro pole vodičů, solenoidů a toroidů.

brief_concepts.name: Biot-Savart law
brief_concepts.definition: The field contribution of an infinitesimal current element.

brief_concepts.name: Ampère's law
brief_concepts.definition: The relation between the field's circulation around a loop and the enclosed current.

brief_concepts.name: Solenoid
brief_concepts.definition: A coil producing a nearly uniform field along its axis.

brief_concepts.name: Magnetic flux
brief_concepts.definition: The amount of magnetic field passing through a surface.

brief_concepts.name: No magnetic monopoles
brief_concepts.definition: The law that magnetic field lines have no sources or sinks, so flux through any closed surface is zero.

new_blocks.name: Magnetism in Matter
new_blocks.description_en: Materials respond to fields through the alignment of atomic magnetic moments, classified as diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic, the last retaining magnetisation below the Curie temperature and underlying permanent magnets.
new_blocks.description_cs: Látky reagují na pole uspořádáním atomárních magnetických momentů a dělí se na diamagnetické, paramagnetické a feromagnetické, přičemž poslední si pod Curieovou teplotou udržují magnetizaci a tvoří základ permanentních magnetů.

brief_concepts.name: Diamagnetism
brief_concepts.definition: Weak repulsion from a field, present in all matter, from induced opposing moments.

brief_concepts.name: Paramagnetism
brief_concepts.definition: Weak attraction from the partial alignment of permanent atomic moments.

brief_concepts.name: Ferromagnetism
brief_concepts.definition: Strong, retained magnetisation from spontaneous alignment in magnetic domains.

brief_concepts.name: Curie temperature
brief_concepts.definition: The temperature above which ferromagnetic order is lost to thermal agitation.

brief_concepts.name: Hysteresis
brief_concepts.definition: The lag of magnetisation behind the applied field, storing energy in magnetic memory.

new_blocks.name: Electromagnetic Induction
new_blocks.description_en: A changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an electromotive force, with the induced current opposing the change; Faraday's law of induction and Lenz's rule govern generators, transformers and inductors.
new_blocks.description_cs: Měnící se magnetický tok obvodem indukuje elektromotorické napětí, přičemž indukovaný proud se změně brání; Faradayův zákon indukce a Lenzovo pravidlo řídí generátory, transformátory a cívky.

brief_concepts.name: Faraday's law
brief_concepts.definition: The induced electromotive force equals minus the rate of change of magnetic flux.

brief_concepts.name: Lenz's law
brief_concepts.definition: The induced current flows so as to oppose the flux change that causes it.

brief_concepts.name: Inductance
brief_concepts.definition: The property relating induced voltage to the rate of change of current.

brief_concepts.name: Transformer
brief_concepts.definition: A device coupling two coils by shared flux to change alternating voltage.

brief_concepts.name: Eddy currents
brief_concepts.definition: Circulating currents induced in bulk conductors by changing fields.

new_blocks.name: Maxwell's Equations
new_blocks.description_en: Four equations — Gauss's laws for electricity and magnetism, Faraday's law, and the Ampère-Maxwell law with its displacement current — unify all classical electromagnetism and predict self-propagating electromagnetic waves.
new_blocks.description_cs: Čtyři rovnice — Gaussovy zákony pro elektřinu a magnetismus, Faradayův zákon a Ampérův–Maxwellův zákon s posuvným proudem — sjednocují celý klasický elektromagnetismus a předpovídají samovolně se šířící elektromagnetické vlny.

brief_concepts.name: Displacement current
brief_concepts.definition: Maxwell's term letting a changing electric field act as a source of magnetic field.

brief_concepts.name: Field unification
brief_concepts.definition: The demonstration that electric and magnetic fields are aspects of one electromagnetic field.

brief_concepts.name: Continuity equation
brief_concepts.definition: Charge conservation implied by the structure of Maxwell's equations.

brief_concepts.name: Electromagnetic potentials
brief_concepts.definition: The scalar and vector potentials from which the fields are derived, with gauge freedom.

brief_concepts.name: Wave prediction
brief_concepts.definition: The result that the equations admit waves travelling at the speed of light.

new_blocks.name: Electromagnetic Waves & Spectrum
new_blocks.description_en: Oscillating electric and magnetic fields propagate as transverse waves at the speed of light, spanning a continuous spectrum from radio to gamma rays and carrying energy and momentum through the Poynting vector and radiation pressure.
new_blocks.description_cs: Kmitající elektrické a magnetické pole se šíří jako příčné vlny rychlostí světla, pokrývají spojité spektrum od rádiových vln po gama záření a přenášejí energii a hybnost prostřednictvím Poyntingova vektoru a tlaku záření.

brief_concepts.name: Speed of light
brief_concepts.definition: The propagation speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum, a universal constant.

brief_concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
brief_concepts.definition: The full range of wavelengths from radio through visible light to gamma rays.

brief_concepts.name: Poynting vector
brief_concepts.definition: The directional energy flux carried by an electromagnetic wave.

brief_concepts.name: Polarization
brief_concepts.definition: The orientation of the wave's electric-field oscillation, linear, circular or elliptical.

brief_concepts.name: Radiation pressure
brief_concepts.definition: The momentum transferred by electromagnetic waves onto surfaces they strike.

new_blocks.name: Reflection, Refraction & Interference
new_blocks.description_en: At boundaries light reflects and refracts according to the laws of reflection and Snell's law, while its wave nature produces interference and diffraction; these govern lenses, mirrors, gratings and imaging.
new_blocks.description_cs: Na rozhraních se světlo odráží a láme podle zákona odrazu a Snellova zákona, zatímco jeho vlnová povaha vytváří interferenci a difrakci; tyto jevy řídí čočky, zrcadla, mřížky a zobrazování.

brief_concepts.name: Snell's law
brief_concepts.definition: The relation between angles of incidence and refraction at a boundary via refractive indices.

brief_concepts.name: Total internal reflection
brief_concepts.definition: Complete reflection above a critical angle, the basis of optical fibres.

brief_concepts.name: Interference
brief_concepts.definition: The superposition of waves producing bright and dark fringes.

brief_concepts.name: Diffraction
brief_concepts.definition: The bending and spreading of waves around obstacles and through apertures.

brief_concepts.name: Dispersion
brief_concepts.definition: The variation of refractive index with wavelength, splitting white light into colours.

new_blocks.name: Dielectrics & Polarization
new_blocks.description_en: An electric field polarises a dielectric by displacing bound charge, weakening the internal field and defining the permittivity; the displacement field D separates free from bound charge in the macroscopic equations.
new_blocks.description_cs: Elektrické pole polarizuje dielektrikum posunutím vázaného náboje, čímž oslabuje vnitřní pole a definuje permitivitu; pole elektrické indukce D odděluje volný náboj od vázaného v makroskopických rovnicích.

brief_concepts.name: Polarization
brief_concepts.definition: The dipole moment per unit volume induced in a dielectric by a field.

brief_concepts.name: Electric displacement
brief_concepts.definition: The field D combining the applied field and the medium's polarization.

brief_concepts.name: Relative permittivity
brief_concepts.definition: The factor by which a dielectric reduces the field, also called the dielectric constant.

brief_concepts.name: Bound charge
brief_concepts.definition: The effective surface and volume charge arising from aligned dipoles.

brief_concepts.name: Dielectric breakdown
brief_concepts.definition: The field strength at which an insulator becomes conducting.

new_blocks.name: Circuit Laws & AC Analysis
new_blocks.description_en: Ohm's law relates voltage, current and resistance, Kirchhoff's laws enforce charge and energy conservation at nodes and loops, and alternating-current analysis uses impedance and phasors to handle capacitors and inductors.
new_blocks.description_cs: Ohmův zákon spojuje napětí, proud a odpor, Kirchhoffovy zákony zajišťují zachování náboje a energie v uzlech a smyčkách a analýza střídavého proudu používá impedanci a fázory k popisu kondenzátorů a cívek.

brief_concepts.name: Ohm's law
brief_concepts.definition: The proportionality of current to voltage through a resistance.

brief_concepts.name: Kirchhoff's laws
brief_concepts.definition: Conservation of current at nodes and of voltage around loops.

brief_concepts.name: Impedance
brief_concepts.definition: The generalisation of resistance to alternating-current circuits with reactance.

brief_concepts.name: Resonance
brief_concepts.definition: The frequency at which an inductor and capacitor exchange energy with minimal impedance.

brief_concepts.name: Power in circuits
brief_concepts.definition: The rate of energy transfer, with real and reactive parts in AC systems.

new_blocks.name: Motors, Generators & Antennas
new_blocks.description_en: Electromagnetic induction and the force on currents underlie machines that convert between electrical and mechanical energy — motors and generators — while accelerating charges in antennas radiate the electromagnetic waves of communication.
new_blocks.description_cs: Elektromagnetická indukce a síla na proudy tvoří základ strojů přeměňujících elektrickou a mechanickou energii — motorů a generátorů — zatímco zrychlované náboje v anténách vyzařují elektromagnetické vlny pro komunikaci.

brief_concepts.name: Electric motor
brief_concepts.definition: A machine converting electrical energy to rotation via force on current loops.

brief_concepts.name: Electric generator
brief_concepts.definition: A machine converting mechanical motion to electricity by induction.

brief_concepts.name: Antenna
brief_concepts.definition: A conductor that radiates or receives electromagnetic waves from accelerating charge.

brief_concepts.name: Waveguide
brief_concepts.definition: A structure that confines and directs electromagnetic waves along its length.

brief_concepts.name: Electromagnetic radiation from acceleration
brief_concepts.definition: The principle that only accelerating charges radiate energy as waves.

new_blocks.name: Postulates & Relativity of Simultaneity
new_blocks.description_en: Special relativity rests on two postulates — the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames and the speed of light is invariant — from which simultaneity becomes relative: events simultaneous in one frame need not be in another.
new_blocks.description_cs: Speciální teorie relativity stojí na dvou postulátech — fyzikální zákony jsou stejné ve všech inerciálních soustavách a rychlost světla je invariantní — z nichž plyne relativita současnosti: události současné v jedné soustavě nemusí být současné v jiné.

brief_concepts.name: Principle of relativity
brief_concepts.definition: The laws of physics take the same form in every inertial frame.

brief_concepts.name: Invariance of light speed
brief_concepts.definition: The speed of light in vacuum is the same for all observers regardless of motion.

brief_concepts.name: Inertial frame
brief_concepts.definition: A reference frame in which a free body moves in a straight line at constant speed.

brief_concepts.name: Relativity of simultaneity
brief_concepts.definition: Whether two separated events are simultaneous depends on the observer's motion.

new_blocks.name: Time Dilation & Length Contraction
new_blocks.description_en: Moving clocks run slow and moving rods contract along their motion, by the Lorentz factor; these reciprocal effects preserve the invariant speed of light and are confirmed by decaying particles and precision clocks.
new_blocks.description_cs: Pohybující se hodiny jdou pomaleji a pohybující se tyče se ve směru pohybu zkracují o Lorentzův faktor; tyto vzájemné jevy zachovávají invariantní rychlost světla a potvrzují je rozpadající se částice a přesné hodiny.

brief_concepts.name: Time dilation
brief_concepts.definition: The slowing of a moving clock as seen from a frame in which it moves.

brief_concepts.name: Length contraction
brief_concepts.definition: The shortening of a moving object along its direction of motion.

brief_concepts.name: Lorentz factor
brief_concepts.definition: The factor gamma quantifying dilation and contraction, growing without bound near light speed.

brief_concepts.name: Proper time
brief_concepts.definition: The time measured by a clock carried along a worldline, an invariant.

brief_concepts.name: Twin paradox
brief_concepts.definition: The asymmetric ageing of a travelling twin, resolved by the acceleration of the return.

new_blocks.name: Lorentz Transformation & Velocity Addition
new_blocks.description_en: The Lorentz transformation mixes space and time coordinates between inertial frames, replacing the Galilean transformation; it yields the relativistic velocity-addition rule that keeps the speed of light as an unreachable limit.
new_blocks.description_cs: Lorentzova transformace mísí prostorové a časové souřadnice mezi inerciálními soustavami a nahrazuje Galileovu transformaci; dává relativistické pravidlo skládání rychlostí, které udržuje rychlost světla jako nedosažitelnou mez.

brief_concepts.name: Lorentz transformation
brief_concepts.definition: The linear transformation of coordinates between inertial frames preserving the light speed.

brief_concepts.name: Velocity addition
brief_concepts.definition: The rule combining velocities so their sum never exceeds the speed of light.

brief_concepts.name: Relativistic Doppler effect
brief_concepts.definition: The frequency shift of light from relative motion, including a transverse component.

brief_concepts.name: Invariant interval
brief_concepts.definition: The spacetime separation of events, agreed on by all inertial observers.

new_blocks.name: Mass-Energy Equivalence
new_blocks.description_en: Energy and mass are equivalent, related by E = mc squared, so a body's rest energy is enormous and any energy has inertia; this underlies nuclear binding energy, particle creation and the energetics of stars.
new_blocks.description_cs: Energie a hmota jsou ekvivalentní, spojené vztahem E = mc na druhou, takže klidová energie tělesa je obrovská a každá energie má setrvačnost; to je základem jaderné vazebné energie, vzniku částic a energetiky hvězd.

brief_concepts.name: Rest energy
brief_concepts.definition: The energy mc squared a body possesses by virtue of its mass alone.

brief_concepts.name: Relativistic momentum
brief_concepts.definition: Momentum that grows faster than velocity and diverges near light speed.

brief_concepts.name: Energy-momentum relation
brief_concepts.definition: The invariant relation E squared = (pc) squared + (mc squared) squared.

brief_concepts.name: Massless particles
brief_concepts.definition: Particles such as photons that carry energy and momentum but no rest mass and move at light speed.

brief_concepts.name: Binding energy
brief_concepts.definition: The mass deficit released when bound systems form, powering nuclear reactions.

new_blocks.name: Minkowski Spacetime & Four-Vectors
new_blocks.description_en: Space and time unite into four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with an indefinite metric; physical quantities become four-vectors and tensors whose invariant magnitudes all observers agree on, making the laws manifestly frame-independent.
new_blocks.description_cs: Prostor a čas se spojují do čtyřrozměrného Minkowského časoprostoru s indefinitní metrikou; fyzikální veličiny se stávají čtyřvektory a tenzory, na jejichž invariantních velikostech se shodnou všichni pozorovatelé, čímž jsou zákony zjevně nezávislé na soustavě.

brief_concepts.name: Minkowski spacetime
brief_concepts.definition: The flat four-dimensional continuum of special relativity with a light-cone structure.

brief_concepts.name: Worldline
brief_concepts.definition: The path of a particle through spacetime.

brief_concepts.name: Light cone
brief_concepts.definition: The surface separating causally connected events from those that cannot interact.

brief_concepts.name: Four-vector
brief_concepts.definition: A four-component quantity transforming under the Lorentz transformation, such as four-momentum.

brief_concepts.name: Causality
brief_concepts.definition: The ordering of cause and effect preserved because no signal outpaces light.

new_blocks.name: Equivalence Principle
new_blocks.description_en: Gravitational and inertial mass are identical, so a freely falling observer feels no gravity and a uniform acceleration is locally indistinguishable from a gravitational field; this equivalence is the seed of general relativity.
new_blocks.description_cs: Gravitační a setrvačná hmotnost jsou totožné, takže volně padající pozorovatel gravitaci necítí a rovnoměrné zrychlení je lokálně nerozlišitelné od gravitačního pole; tato ekvivalence je zárodkem obecné teorie relativity.

brief_concepts.name: Equivalence principle
brief_concepts.definition: The local equivalence of a gravitational field and an accelerating frame.

brief_concepts.name: Free fall
brief_concepts.definition: Motion under gravity alone, in which an observer feels weightless.

brief_concepts.name: Gravitational time dilation
brief_concepts.definition: The slowing of clocks deeper in a gravitational potential.

brief_concepts.name: Gravitational redshift
brief_concepts.definition: The lengthening of a photon's wavelength as it climbs out of a gravity well.

new_blocks.name: Curved Spacetime & Field Equations
new_blocks.description_en: Gravity is the curvature of spacetime produced by energy and momentum; matter tells spacetime how to curve through Einstein's field equations, and spacetime tells matter how to move along geodesics.
new_blocks.description_cs: Gravitace je zakřivení časoprostoru způsobené energií a hybností; hmota určuje, jak se má časoprostor zakřivit, prostřednictvím Einsteinových rovnic pole, a časoprostor určuje hmotě, jak se má pohybovat po geodetikách.

brief_concepts.name: Spacetime curvature
brief_concepts.definition: The geometric deviation from flatness that manifests as gravity.

brief_concepts.name: Geodesic
brief_concepts.definition: The straightest possible path in curved spacetime, followed by free-falling bodies.

brief_concepts.name: Einstein field equations
brief_concepts.definition: The equations relating spacetime curvature to the energy-momentum of matter.

brief_concepts.name: Metric tensor
brief_concepts.definition: The field encoding distances and times, the dynamical variable of general relativity.

brief_concepts.name: Cosmological constant
brief_concepts.definition: A uniform energy of space driving accelerated expansion, added to the field equations.

new_blocks.name: Black Holes
new_blocks.description_en: When gravity overwhelms all support, matter collapses to a region from which not even light escapes, bounded by an event horizon and characterised by mass, charge and spin; observations confirm them at stellar and galactic scales.
new_blocks.description_cs: Když gravitace přemůže veškerou oporu, hmota se zhroutí do oblasti, z níž neunikne ani světlo, ohraničené horizontem událostí a charakterizované hmotností, nábojem a rotací; pozorování je potvrzují na hvězdných i galaktických škálách.

brief_concepts.name: Event horizon
brief_concepts.definition: The boundary beyond which no signal can escape a black hole.

brief_concepts.name: Schwarzschild solution
brief_concepts.definition: The exact spacetime of a non-rotating spherical mass.

brief_concepts.name: Singularity
brief_concepts.definition: The region of formally infinite curvature at a black hole's centre, where the theory breaks down.

brief_concepts.name: Kerr solution
brief_concepts.definition: The spacetime of a rotating black hole, dragging spacetime around it.

brief_concepts.name: Hawking radiation
brief_concepts.definition: The predicted thermal emission that lets black holes slowly evaporate.

new_blocks.name: Gravitational Waves
new_blocks.description_en: Accelerating masses radiate ripples of spacetime curvature travelling at the speed of light; first detected in 2015 from merging black holes, they open a new observational window on the most violent events in the universe.
new_blocks.description_cs: Zrychlující se hmoty vyzařují vlnění zakřivení časoprostoru šířící se rychlostí světla; poprvé detekované v roce 2015 ze splývajících černých děr otevírají nové pozorovací okno na nejprudší děje ve vesmíru.

brief_concepts.name: Gravitational wave
brief_concepts.definition: A propagating oscillation of spacetime curvature emitted by accelerating masses.

brief_concepts.name: Binary inspiral
brief_concepts.definition: The spiralling merger of two compact objects, a strong wave source.

brief_concepts.name: Interferometric detection
brief_concepts.definition: The measurement of tiny length changes by laser interferometers such as LIGO.

brief_concepts.name: Multi-messenger astronomy
brief_concepts.definition: The combined observation of gravitational waves and electromagnetic or particle signals.

new_blocks.name: Classical Tests of Relativity
new_blocks.description_en: General relativity was confirmed by the anomalous precession of Mercury's perihelion, the bending of starlight by the Sun, and the gravitational redshift of light, and continues to pass ever more precise experimental tests.
new_blocks.description_cs: Obecná teorie relativity byla potvrzena anomálním stáčením perihelia Merkuru, ohybem hvězdného světla Sluncem a gravitačním rudým posuvem světla a nadále obstává ve stále přesnějších experimentálních testech.

brief_concepts.name: Perihelion precession
brief_concepts.definition: The excess rotation of Mercury's orbit explained by general relativity.

brief_concepts.name: Light deflection
brief_concepts.definition: The bending of light by mass, first measured during a solar eclipse.

brief_concepts.name: Shapiro delay
brief_concepts.definition: The extra travel time of light passing near a massive body.

brief_concepts.name: Frame dragging
brief_concepts.definition: The twisting of spacetime by a rotating mass, measured by orbiting gyroscopes.

new_blocks.name: Relativity in Navigation & Technology
new_blocks.description_en: Satellite navigation must correct for both special-relativistic time dilation from orbital speed and general-relativistic speed-up from weaker gravity, without which position errors would accumulate at kilometres per day.
new_blocks.description_cs: Družicová navigace musí korigovat jak speciálně-relativistickou dilataci času z orbitální rychlosti, tak obecně-relativistické zrychlení hodin ze slabší gravitace, bez čehož by chyby polohy narůstaly o kilometry za den.

brief_concepts.name: GPS time correction
brief_concepts.definition: The net relativistic clock adjustment applied to navigation satellites.

brief_concepts.name: Orbital time dilation
brief_concepts.definition: The special-relativistic slowing of a fast-moving satellite clock.

brief_concepts.name: Altitude clock speed-up
brief_concepts.definition: The general-relativistic quickening of a clock in weaker gravity.

brief_concepts.name: Precision timekeeping
brief_concepts.definition: The use of relativity in atomic clocks and geodesy at sub-nanosecond accuracy.

new_blocks.name: Nucleons & Binding Energy
new_blocks.description_en: The nucleus is bound protons and neutrons held by the strong nuclear force; the binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron, explaining why fusion of light nuclei and fission of heavy ones both release energy.
new_blocks.description_cs: Jádro tvoří vázané protony a neutrony držené silnou jadernou silou; vazebná energie na nukleon dosahuje maxima poblíž železa, což vysvětluje, proč fúze lehkých jader i štěpení těžkých uvolňují energii.

brief_concepts.name: Nucleon
brief_concepts.definition: A proton or neutron, the constituents of the nucleus.

brief_concepts.name: Strong nuclear force
brief_concepts.definition: The short-range attraction binding nucleons against electrostatic repulsion.

brief_concepts.name: Binding energy
brief_concepts.definition: The energy needed to disassemble a nucleus, reflected in a mass deficit.

brief_concepts.name: Mass defect
brief_concepts.definition: The difference between a nucleus's mass and the sum of its free nucleons.

brief_concepts.name: Binding-energy curve
brief_concepts.definition: The variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number, peaking at iron.

new_blocks.name: Nuclear Models
new_blocks.description_en: Complementary models capture nuclear behaviour: the liquid-drop model explains binding and fission energetics, while the shell model explains magic numbers and spins through nucleons filling quantised energy levels.
new_blocks.description_cs: Doplňující se modely popisují chování jádra: kapkový model vysvětluje vazebnou energii a energetiku štěpení, zatímco slupkový model vysvětluje magická čísla a spiny pomocí nukleonů zaplňujících kvantované energetické hladiny.

brief_concepts.name: Liquid-drop model
brief_concepts.definition: A model treating the nucleus as an incompressible charged drop.

brief_concepts.name: Semi-empirical mass formula
brief_concepts.definition: The formula estimating binding energy from volume, surface, Coulomb and other terms.

brief_concepts.name: Shell model
brief_concepts.definition: A model of nucleons in quantised orbitals explaining stability patterns.

brief_concepts.name: Magic numbers
brief_concepts.definition: Nucleon counts giving closed shells and exceptional stability.

brief_concepts.name: Nuclear spin
brief_concepts.definition: The total angular momentum of a nucleus, important in magnetic resonance.

new_blocks.name: Modes of Radioactive Decay
new_blocks.description_en: Unstable nuclei shed energy by emitting an alpha particle, converting a neutron and proton through beta decay, or releasing a gamma photon; each mode changes the nucleus in a characteristic way governed by conservation laws.
new_blocks.description_cs: Nestabilní jádra se zbavují energie vyzářením částice alfa, přeměnou neutronu a protonu při beta rozpadu nebo uvolněním fotonu gama; každý způsob mění jádro charakteristickým způsobem daným zákony zachování.

brief_concepts.name: Alpha decay
brief_concepts.definition: Emission of a helium nucleus, reducing mass number by four.

brief_concepts.name: Beta decay
brief_concepts.definition: Conversion of a neutron to a proton or vice versa, emitting an electron or positron and a neutrino.

brief_concepts.name: Gamma decay
brief_concepts.definition: Emission of a high-energy photon as an excited nucleus relaxes.

brief_concepts.name: Electron capture
brief_concepts.definition: Absorption of an inner electron converting a proton to a neutron.

brief_concepts.name: Q-value
brief_concepts.definition: The energy released in a decay, shared as kinetic energy of the products.

new_blocks.name: Decay Law, Half-Life & Dating
new_blocks.description_en: Radioactive decay is a random process with a fixed probability per unit time, giving exponential decay and a characteristic half-life; the steady clock this provides underlies radiometric dating and radioactive tracing.
new_blocks.description_cs: Radioaktivní rozpad je náhodný děj s pevnou pravděpodobností za jednotku času, což vede k exponenciálnímu poklesu a charakteristickému poločasu rozpadu; tyto stálé hodiny jsou základem radiometrického datování a radioaktivního značkování.

brief_concepts.name: Half-life
brief_concepts.definition: The time for half the nuclei in a sample to decay.

brief_concepts.name: Exponential decay law
brief_concepts.definition: The rule that activity falls off exponentially with time.

brief_concepts.name: Activity
brief_concepts.definition: The number of decays per unit time in a radioactive sample.

brief_concepts.name: Decay chain
brief_concepts.definition: A sequence of decays leading from an unstable parent to a stable end nucleus.

brief_concepts.name: Radiometric dating
brief_concepts.definition: Determining age from the ratio of parent to daughter isotopes, as in carbon-14 dating.

new_blocks.name: Reactions & Cross Sections
new_blocks.description_en: In a nuclear reaction incident particles transform a target nucleus, conserving nucleon number, charge, energy and momentum; the cross section quantifies reaction probability, peaking sharply at resonances.
new_blocks.description_cs: Při jaderné reakci dopadající částice přeměňují terčové jádro za zachování počtu nukleonů, náboje, energie a hybnosti; účinný průřez udává pravděpodobnost reakce a dosahuje ostrých maxim při rezonancích.

brief_concepts.name: Cross section
brief_concepts.definition: The effective target area measuring the probability of a nuclear reaction.

brief_concepts.name: Reaction kinematics
brief_concepts.definition: The application of energy and momentum conservation to reaction products.

brief_concepts.name: Compound nucleus
brief_concepts.definition: A short-lived excited nucleus formed and then decaying during a reaction.

brief_concepts.name: Resonance
brief_concepts.definition: A sharp peak in cross section when the energy matches a nuclear excited state.

brief_concepts.name: Transmutation
brief_concepts.definition: The conversion of one element into another by a nuclear reaction.

new_blocks.name: Nuclear Fission
new_blocks.description_en: A heavy nucleus splits into lighter fragments, releasing energy and free neutrons that can sustain a chain reaction; controlled in reactors by moderators and control rods, uncontrolled it drives fission weapons.
new_blocks.description_cs: Těžké jádro se rozštěpí na lehčí fragmenty, přičemž uvolní energii a volné neutrony schopné udržet řetězovou reakci; v reaktorech se řídí moderátory a regulačními tyčemi, neřízené pohání štěpné zbraně.

brief_concepts.name: Induced fission
brief_concepts.definition: Splitting of a heavy nucleus triggered by neutron absorption.

brief_concepts.name: Chain reaction
brief_concepts.definition: A self-sustaining sequence in which fission neutrons induce further fissions.

brief_concepts.name: Critical mass
brief_concepts.definition: The minimum amount of fissile material needed to sustain a chain reaction.

brief_concepts.name: Moderator
brief_concepts.definition: A material slowing neutrons to increase the fission probability in a reactor.

brief_concepts.name: Fission products
brief_concepts.definition: The radioactive fragments and neutrons produced by fission.

new_blocks.name: Nuclear Fusion
new_blocks.description_en: Light nuclei merge into a heavier one, releasing large energy per nucleon but requiring immense temperature and pressure to overcome their electrostatic repulsion; fusion powers the stars and is pursued for terrestrial energy.
new_blocks.description_cs: Lehká jádra se slučují do těžšího a uvolňují velkou energii na nukleon, avšak vyžadují obrovskou teplotu a tlak k překonání elektrostatického odpuzování; fúze pohání hvězdy a usiluje se o ni jako o pozemský zdroj energie.

brief_concepts.name: Fusion reaction
brief_concepts.definition: The merging of light nuclei into a heavier one with energy release.

brief_concepts.name: Coulomb barrier
brief_concepts.definition: The electrostatic repulsion that fusing nuclei must overcome.

brief_concepts.name: Thermonuclear ignition
brief_concepts.definition: The condition where fusion becomes self-sustaining through its own heat.

brief_concepts.name: Magnetic confinement
brief_concepts.definition: Holding hot plasma with magnetic fields, as in a tokamak.

brief_concepts.name: Inertial confinement
brief_concepts.definition: Compressing fuel by lasers or beams to reach fusion conditions.

new_blocks.name: Nuclear Medicine & Radiation Detection
new_blocks.description_en: Radioactive isotopes and radiation are harnessed for imaging and therapy and detected by instruments that convert ionisation into measurable signals; radiation protection limits exposure through shielding, distance and time.
new_blocks.description_cs: Radioaktivní izotopy a záření se využívají k zobrazování a léčbě a detekují je přístroje, které převádějí ionizaci na měřitelný signál; radiační ochrana omezuje ozáření pomocí stínění, vzdálenosti a času.

brief_concepts.name: Radiotracer
brief_concepts.definition: A radioactive label following a substance through a body or system.

brief_concepts.name: Positron emission tomography
brief_concepts.definition: Imaging that reconstructs positron-emitter distribution in the body.

brief_concepts.name: Radiotherapy
brief_concepts.definition: The use of ionising radiation to destroy diseased tissue.

brief_concepts.name: Geiger counter
brief_concepts.definition: A detector registering individual ionising events as pulses.

brief_concepts.name: Radiation protection
brief_concepts.definition: Limiting dose through shielding, distance and exposure time.

new_blocks.name: Nucleosynthesis
new_blocks.description_en: The chemical elements are forged by nuclear reactions: the lightest in the first minutes of the Big Bang, heavier ones by fusion in stellar cores, and the heaviest by rapid neutron capture in supernovae and neutron-star mergers.
new_blocks.description_cs: Chemické prvky vznikají jadernými reakcemi: nejlehčí v prvních minutách velkého třesku, těžší fúzí v jádrech hvězd a nejtěžší rychlým záchytem neutronů v supernovách a při splývání neutronových hvězd.

brief_concepts.name: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
brief_concepts.definition: The formation of hydrogen, helium and lithium in the early universe.

brief_concepts.name: Stellar nucleosynthesis
brief_concepts.definition: The building of elements up to iron by fusion in stars.

brief_concepts.name: s-process
brief_concepts.definition: Slow neutron capture building heavy nuclei in evolved stars.

brief_concepts.name: r-process
brief_concepts.definition: Rapid neutron capture forming the heaviest elements in explosive events.

brief_concepts.name: Cosmic abundance
brief_concepts.definition: The observed proportions of the elements set by these processes.

new_blocks.name: Quarks & Leptons
new_blocks.description_en: Matter is built from two families of spin-half fermions: six quarks, which combine into protons, neutrons and other hadrons, and six leptons, including the electron and its neutrino, arranged in three generations of increasing mass.
new_blocks.description_cs: Hmota je tvořena dvěma rodinami fermionů se spinem jedna polovina: šesti kvarky, které se skládají do protonů, neutronů a dalších hadronů, a šesti leptony, mezi něž patří elektron a jeho neutrino, uspořádanými do tří generací s rostoucí hmotností.

brief_concepts.name: Quark
brief_concepts.definition: A fermion carrying colour charge that combines to form hadrons, never seen in isolation.

brief_concepts.name: Lepton
brief_concepts.definition: A fermion without colour charge, such as the electron, muon, tau and their neutrinos.

brief_concepts.name: Generations
brief_concepts.definition: The three families of quarks and leptons, differing mainly in mass.

brief_concepts.name: Hadron
brief_concepts.definition: A composite particle of quarks bound by the strong force, either a baryon or a meson.

brief_concepts.name: Antiparticle
brief_concepts.definition: A partner with opposite charges to a given particle, produced together with it.

new_blocks.name: Gauge Bosons & the Higgs
new_blocks.description_en: Forces are carried by spin-one gauge bosons — the photon, the gluons and the W and Z — while the spin-zero Higgs boson, discovered in 2012, arises from the field whose interaction endows particles with mass.
