new_blocks.description_cs: Síly přenášejí kalibrační bosony se spinem jedna — foton, gluony a bosony W a Z — zatímco Higgsův boson se spinem nula, objevený v roce 2012, pochází z pole, jehož interakce dodává částicím hmotnost.

brief_concepts.name: Photon
brief_concepts.definition: The massless carrier of the electromagnetic force.

brief_concepts.name: Gluon
brief_concepts.definition: The carrier of the strong force, itself colour-charged.

brief_concepts.name: W and Z bosons
brief_concepts.definition: The massive carriers of the weak force.

brief_concepts.name: Higgs boson
brief_concepts.definition: The excitation of the Higgs field, confirmed in 2012.

brief_concepts.name: Higgs mechanism
brief_concepts.definition: The process giving mass to the weak bosons and fermions through symmetry breaking.

new_blocks.name: Quantum Electrodynamics & Chromodynamics
new_blocks.description_en: Quantum electrodynamics describes the electromagnetic interaction of charged particles by photon exchange to extraordinary precision, while quantum chromodynamics describes the strong force among quarks and gluons, with confinement and asymptotic freedom.
new_blocks.description_cs: Kvantová elektrodynamika popisuje elektromagnetickou interakci nabitých částic výměnou fotonů s mimořádnou přesností, zatímco kvantová chromodynamika popisuje silnou sílu mezi kvarky a gluony s uvězněním a asymptotickou volností.

brief_concepts.name: Quantum electrodynamics
brief_concepts.definition: The quantum field theory of light and charged matter, tested to extreme precision.

brief_concepts.name: Feynman diagram
brief_concepts.definition: A pictorial term in the perturbative expansion of a scattering amplitude.

brief_concepts.name: Colour charge
brief_concepts.definition: The strong-force analogue of electric charge, carried by quarks and gluons.

brief_concepts.name: Confinement
brief_concepts.definition: The property that colour-charged particles cannot exist in isolation.

brief_concepts.name: Asymptotic freedom
brief_concepts.definition: The weakening of the strong force at short distances and high energies.

new_blocks.name: Weak Interaction & Electroweak Unification
new_blocks.description_en: The weak interaction changes particle flavour and causes beta decay through massive W and Z bosons; at high energy it merges with electromagnetism into a single electroweak force, unified in the Standard Model.
new_blocks.description_cs: Slabá interakce mění vůni částic a způsobuje beta rozpad prostřednictvím hmotných bosonů W a Z; při vysokých energiích splývá s elektromagnetismem do jediné elektroslabé síly sjednocené ve standardním modelu.

brief_concepts.name: Weak interaction
brief_concepts.definition: The short-range force responsible for flavour change and beta decay.

brief_concepts.name: Flavour change
brief_concepts.definition: The conversion of one quark or lepton type into another via the weak force.

brief_concepts.name: Electroweak unification
brief_concepts.definition: The theory merging electromagnetism and the weak force at high energy.

brief_concepts.name: Neutrino interaction
brief_concepts.definition: The exclusively weak coupling that makes neutrinos so penetrating.

brief_concepts.name: Parity violation
brief_concepts.definition: The weak force's distinction between left- and right-handed particles.

new_blocks.name: Symmetries & Conservation
new_blocks.description_en: Every continuous symmetry implies a conserved quantity by Noether's theorem, so energy, momentum and charge conservation reflect symmetries of space, time and gauge; particle physics is organised around such symmetry principles.
new_blocks.description_cs: Každá spojitá symetrie implikuje zachovávanou veličinu podle Noetherové věty, takže zachování energie, hybnosti a náboje odráží symetrie prostoru, času a kalibrace; částicová fyzika je uspořádána kolem takových principů symetrie.

brief_concepts.name: Noether's theorem
brief_concepts.definition: The correspondence between continuous symmetries and conservation laws.

brief_concepts.name: Gauge symmetry
brief_concepts.definition: The local symmetry underlying each fundamental interaction.

brief_concepts.name: Conserved quantum numbers
brief_concepts.definition: Quantities such as baryon and lepton number preserved in interactions.

brief_concepts.name: Isospin
brief_concepts.definition: An approximate symmetry treating protons and neutrons as two states of one particle.

brief_concepts.name: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
brief_concepts.definition: A symmetric theory with an asymmetric ground state, central to mass generation.

new_blocks.name: Discrete Symmetries & CP Violation
new_blocks.description_en: The discrete operations of charge conjugation, parity and time reversal are individually violated by the weak force; their combination CPT is exact, and CP violation is essential to explaining why the universe contains more matter than antimatter.
new_blocks.description_cs: Diskrétní operace nábojového sdružení, parity a obrácení času jsou jednotlivě narušovány slabou silou; jejich kombinace CPT je přesná a narušení CP je klíčové pro vysvětlení, proč vesmír obsahuje více hmoty než antihmoty.

brief_concepts.name: Parity
brief_concepts.definition: The symmetry under spatial reflection, violated by the weak interaction.

brief_concepts.name: Charge conjugation
brief_concepts.definition: The operation exchanging particles with their antiparticles.

brief_concepts.name: CP violation
brief_concepts.definition: The small asymmetry between matter and antimatter behaviour.

brief_concepts.name: CPT theorem
brief_concepts.definition: The exact combined symmetry required by relativistic quantum field theory.

brief_concepts.name: Baryon asymmetry
brief_concepts.definition: The cosmic excess of matter over antimatter that CP violation helps explain.

new_blocks.name: Accelerators & Colliders
new_blocks.description_en: Particle accelerators raise charged particles to high energy with electric and magnetic fields and collide them to create new particles from energy; colliders such as the Large Hadron Collider probe the smallest scales.
new_blocks.description_cs: Urychlovače částic zvyšují energii nabitých částic pomocí elektrických a magnetických polí a srážejí je, aby z energie vznikaly nové částice; srážeče, jako je Velký hadronový srážeč, zkoumají nejmenší škály.

brief_concepts.name: Particle accelerator
brief_concepts.definition: A machine boosting charged particles to high energy using electromagnetic fields.

brief_concepts.name: Collider
brief_concepts.definition: An accelerator crossing two beams to maximise collision energy.

brief_concepts.name: Centre-of-mass energy
brief_concepts.definition: The energy available in a collision to create new particles.

brief_concepts.name: Synchrotron
brief_concepts.definition: A circular accelerator with fields ramped in step with rising particle energy.

brief_concepts.name: Luminosity
brief_concepts.definition: The measure of collision rate determining how often rare processes occur.

new_blocks.name: Detectors & Discovery
new_blocks.description_en: Layered detectors track charged particles, measure their momentum and energy, and identify them by their signatures; a discovery is claimed only when a signal exceeds background at the stringent five-sigma statistical level.
new_blocks.description_cs: Vrstvené detektory sledují nabité částice, měří jejich hybnost a energii a identifikují je podle jejich signatur; objev se prohlašuje teprve tehdy, když signál překročí pozadí na přísné statistické úrovni pěti sigma.

brief_concepts.name: Tracking detector
brief_concepts.definition: A device recording the paths of charged particles in a magnetic field.

brief_concepts.name: Calorimeter
brief_concepts.definition: A detector measuring particle energy by absorbing it in dense material.

brief_concepts.name: Particle identification
brief_concepts.definition: Distinguishing particle types from their tracks and energy deposits.

brief_concepts.name: Five-sigma criterion
brief_concepts.definition: The statistical threshold conventionally required to claim a discovery.

brief_concepts.name: Background rejection
brief_concepts.definition: The removal of known processes to isolate a sought-after signal.

new_blocks.name: Neutrino Physics
new_blocks.description_en: Neutrinos oscillate between flavours as they travel, proving they have tiny nonzero masses unexplained by the Standard Model; their nature, mass ordering and possible role in matter-antimatter asymmetry are active frontiers.
new_blocks.description_cs: Neutrina během letu oscilují mezi vůněmi, což dokazuje, že mají nepatrné nenulové hmotnosti, jež standardní model nevysvětluje; jejich povaha, uspořádání hmotností a možná role v asymetrii hmoty a antihmoty jsou aktivní hranice výzkumu.

brief_concepts.name: Neutrino oscillation
brief_concepts.definition: The periodic change of neutrino flavour in flight, implying nonzero mass.

brief_concepts.name: Mass hierarchy
brief_concepts.definition: The unknown ordering of the three neutrino mass states.

brief_concepts.name: Majorana neutrino
brief_concepts.definition: The open possibility that the neutrino is its own antiparticle.

brief_concepts.name: Sterile neutrino
brief_concepts.definition: A hypothesised neutrino interacting only through gravity and mixing.

brief_concepts.name: Neutrinoless double beta decay
brief_concepts.definition: A sought-after rare process that would reveal a Majorana nature.

new_blocks.name: Dark Matter, Supersymmetry & Unification
new_blocks.description_en: The Standard Model omits gravity, dark matter and the origin of its parameters; proposed extensions include supersymmetry, grand unified theories merging the forces, and candidate dark-matter particles, none yet confirmed.
new_blocks.description_cs: Standardní model opomíjí gravitaci, temnou hmotu a původ svých parametrů; navrhovaná rozšíření zahrnují supersymetrii, teorie velkého sjednocení slučující síly a kandidátní částice temné hmoty, žádné však dosud nebylo potvrzeno.

brief_concepts.name: Dark matter
brief_concepts.definition: The unseen mass whose gravity shapes galaxies, of unknown particle identity.

brief_concepts.name: Supersymmetry
brief_concepts.definition: A proposed symmetry pairing fermions with bosons, so far unobserved.

brief_concepts.name: Grand unified theory
brief_concepts.definition: A theory merging the strong, weak and electromagnetic forces at high energy.

brief_concepts.name: Hierarchy problem
brief_concepts.definition: The puzzle of why the Higgs mass is so far below the unification scale.

brief_concepts.name: Proton decay
brief_concepts.definition: A predicted rare decay of the proton in many unified theories, not yet seen.

new_blocks.name: Stellar Structure & Energy Generation
new_blocks.description_en: A star is a self-gravitating ball of plasma in hydrostatic equilibrium, its inward gravity balanced by outward pressure sustained by nuclear fusion in the core; energy flows outward by radiation and convection to the surface.
new_blocks.description_cs: Hvězda je samogravitující koule plazmatu v hydrostatické rovnováze, jejíž dovnitř mířící gravitaci vyvažuje ven mířící tlak udržovaný jadernou fúzí v jádru; energie proudí ven zářením a konvekcí k povrchu.

brief_concepts.name: Hydrostatic equilibrium
brief_concepts.definition: The balance between gravity and pressure that keeps a star stable.

brief_concepts.name: Proton-proton chain
brief_concepts.definition: The dominant hydrogen-fusion sequence powering low-mass stars.

brief_concepts.name: CNO cycle
brief_concepts.definition: A catalytic hydrogen-fusion cycle dominant in more massive stars.

brief_concepts.name: Radiative and convective transport
brief_concepts.definition: The two ways energy moves from a star's core to its surface.

brief_concepts.name: Luminosity
brief_concepts.definition: The total power a star radiates, set by its mass and structure.

new_blocks.name: Stellar Evolution
new_blocks.description_en: Stars evolve as they exhaust their nuclear fuel, moving off the main sequence to become giants and shedding or exploding their outer layers; the mass of a star determines its lifetime and its final fate.
new_blocks.description_cs: Hvězdy se vyvíjejí, jak spotřebovávají jaderné palivo, opouštějí hlavní posloupnost, stávají se obry a odvrhávají nebo vybuchují své vnější vrstvy; hmotnost hvězdy určuje její délku života i konečný osud.

brief_concepts.name: Main sequence
brief_concepts.definition: The long stable phase of core hydrogen fusion where most stars spend their lives.

brief_concepts.name: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
brief_concepts.definition: The plot of luminosity against temperature mapping stellar populations.

brief_concepts.name: Red giant phase
brief_concepts.definition: The swelling of a star after core hydrogen is exhausted.

brief_concepts.name: Planetary nebula
brief_concepts.definition: The ejected envelope of a dying low-mass star, leaving a white dwarf.

brief_concepts.name: Mass-lifetime relation
brief_concepts.definition: The rule that more massive stars burn brighter and die far sooner.

new_blocks.name: White Dwarfs & Neutron Stars
new_blocks.description_en: White dwarfs and neutron stars are the collapsed cores of dead stars, held up by electron and neutron degeneracy pressure respectively; each has a maximum mass beyond which collapse continues, the Chandrasekhar and Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limits.
new_blocks.description_cs: Bílí trpaslíci a neutronové hvězdy jsou zhroucená jádra mrtvých hvězd, držená degeneračním tlakem elektronů, respektive neutronů; každý má maximální hmotnost, za níž kolaps pokračuje — Chandrasekharovu a Tolmanovu–Oppenheimerovu–Volkoffovu mez.

brief_concepts.name: Degeneracy pressure
brief_concepts.definition: The quantum pressure from the exclusion principle supporting compact stars.

brief_concepts.name: Chandrasekhar limit
brief_concepts.definition: The maximum mass of a white dwarf, about 1.4 solar masses.

brief_concepts.name: Neutron star
brief_concepts.definition: An ultradense stellar remnant composed largely of neutrons.

brief_concepts.name: Pulsar
brief_concepts.definition: A rapidly rotating magnetised neutron star seen as pulses of radiation.

brief_concepts.name: Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit
brief_concepts.definition: The maximum mass of a neutron star before black-hole collapse.

new_blocks.name: Stellar Black Holes & Accretion
new_blocks.description_en: When collapse exceeds all support a stellar black hole forms; matter falling onto compact objects releases enormous energy as it forms a hot accretion disc, making X-ray binaries and quasars among the brightest sources in the sky.
new_blocks.description_cs: Když kolaps překročí veškerou oporu, vzniká hvězdná černá díra; hmota padající na kompaktní objekty uvolňuje při tvorbě horkého akrečního disku obrovskou energii, což činí z rentgenových dvojhvězd a kvasarů jedny z nejjasnějších zdrojů na obloze.

brief_concepts.name: Stellar black hole
brief_concepts.definition: A black hole formed by the collapse of a massive star's core.

brief_concepts.name: Accretion disc
brief_concepts.definition: A disc of infalling matter heated to radiate as it spirals inward.

brief_concepts.name: X-ray binary
brief_concepts.definition: A compact object accreting from a companion star, bright in X-rays.

brief_concepts.name: Relativistic jet
brief_concepts.definition: A collimated outflow launched from near an accreting compact object.

brief_concepts.name: Eddington limit
brief_concepts.definition: The luminosity at which radiation pressure halts further accretion.

new_blocks.name: The Interstellar Medium
new_blocks.description_en: The space between stars holds gas and dust in phases from cold molecular clouds to hot ionised plasma, enriched by stellar death and cycled into new stars; its physics governs cooling, heating and the chemistry of space.
new_blocks.description_cs: Prostor mezi hvězdami obsahuje plyn a prach ve fázích od chladných molekulárních mračen po horké ionizované plazma, obohacovaný zánikem hvězd a znovu zapojovaný do nových hvězd; jeho fyzika řídí ochlazování, ohřev a chemii vesmíru.

brief_concepts.name: Molecular cloud
brief_concepts.definition: A cold dense region of gas where stars form.

brief_concepts.name: Interstellar dust
brief_concepts.definition: Fine solid grains that redden starlight and seed molecule formation.

brief_concepts.name: Ionised gas
brief_concepts.definition: Hot plasma around massive stars, glowing as emission nebulae.

brief_concepts.name: Interstellar extinction
brief_concepts.definition: The dimming and reddening of starlight by intervening dust.

brief_concepts.name: Cosmic cycle of matter
brief_concepts.definition: The recycling of gas from dying stars into new generations.

new_blocks.name: Star Formation
new_blocks.description_en: Stars are born when a molecular cloud becomes gravitationally unstable and fragments and collapses, forming protostars that accrete through discs and ignite fusion once their cores reach the required temperature.
new_blocks.description_cs: Hvězdy se rodí, když se molekulární mračno stane gravitačně nestabilním, rozpadne se a zhroutí, přičemž vznikají protohvězdy, které akreují skrze disky a zažehnou fúzi, jakmile jejich jádra dosáhnou potřebné teploty.

brief_concepts.name: Jeans instability
brief_concepts.definition: The condition under which a gas cloud collapses under its own gravity.

brief_concepts.name: Protostar
brief_concepts.definition: A forming star still accreting from its birth cloud.

brief_concepts.name: Protoplanetary disc
brief_concepts.definition: The disc of gas and dust around a young star from which planets form.

brief_concepts.name: Initial mass function
brief_concepts.definition: The distribution of masses with which stars are born.

brief_concepts.name: Bipolar outflow
brief_concepts.definition: The jets of gas ejected along the poles of a forming star.

new_blocks.name: Galaxy Dynamics & Dark Matter
new_blocks.description_en: Galaxies are gravitationally bound systems of stars, gas and dark matter; their flat rotation curves reveal far more mass than the visible stars provide, the primary evidence for dark matter haloes surrounding them.
new_blocks.description_cs: Galaxie jsou gravitačně vázané soustavy hvězd, plynu a temné hmoty; jejich ploché rotační křivky odhalují mnohem více hmoty, než poskytují viditelné hvězdy, což je hlavní důkaz pro halo temné hmoty, jež je obklopují.

brief_concepts.name: Rotation curve
brief_concepts.definition: The orbital speed of stars versus distance from a galaxy's centre.

brief_concepts.name: Dark matter halo
brief_concepts.definition: The extended invisible mass whose gravity binds a galaxy.

brief_concepts.name: Galaxy morphology
brief_concepts.definition: The classification of galaxies as spiral, elliptical or irregular.

brief_concepts.name: Galactic dynamics
brief_concepts.definition: The gravitational motion of stars and gas within a galaxy.

brief_concepts.name: Galaxy mergers
brief_concepts.definition: The collisions that reshape galaxies and trigger star formation.

new_blocks.name: Active Galactic Nuclei & Large-Scale Structure
new_blocks.description_en: A supermassive black hole accreting at a galaxy's centre powers active galactic nuclei and quasars, while galaxies themselves cluster into filaments and voids forming the cosmic web, the largest structure in the universe.
new_blocks.description_cs: Supermasivní černá díra akreující ve středu galaxie pohání aktivní galaktická jádra a kvasary, zatímco samotné galaxie se shlukují do vláken a prázdnot tvořících kosmickou síť, největší strukturu ve vesmíru.

brief_concepts.name: Supermassive black hole
brief_concepts.definition: The million-to-billion-solar-mass black hole at a galaxy's core.

brief_concepts.name: Quasar
brief_concepts.definition: An extremely luminous active galactic nucleus in the distant universe.

brief_concepts.name: Galaxy cluster
brief_concepts.definition: A gravitationally bound assembly of hundreds to thousands of galaxies.

brief_concepts.name: Cosmic web
brief_concepts.definition: The filamentary large-scale arrangement of galaxies and dark matter.

brief_concepts.name: Gravitational lensing
brief_concepts.definition: The bending of light by mass, used to map dark matter and magnify distant sources.

new_blocks.name: Supernovae & Cosmic Rays
new_blocks.description_en: Massive stars end in supernova explosions that disperse newly forged elements and drive shock waves accelerating cosmic rays — high-energy particles that pervade the galaxy and strike the Earth's atmosphere.
new_blocks.description_cs: Hmotné hvězdy končí výbuchy supernov, které rozptylují nově vytvořené prvky a vytvářejí rázové vlny urychlující kosmické záření — vysokoenergetické částice, jež prostupují galaxií a dopadají na zemskou atmosféru.

brief_concepts.name: Core-collapse supernova
brief_concepts.definition: The explosion of a massive star when its iron core collapses.

brief_concepts.name: Type Ia supernova
brief_concepts.definition: The thermonuclear detonation of a white dwarf, a cosmic standard candle.

brief_concepts.name: Supernova remnant
brief_concepts.definition: The expanding shocked shell left by a supernova.

brief_concepts.name: Cosmic rays
brief_concepts.definition: High-energy charged particles from space, accelerated by shocks and other sources.

brief_concepts.name: Shock acceleration
brief_concepts.definition: The mechanism boosting particles to high energy at astrophysical shock fronts.

new_blocks.name: Multi-Messenger Astrophysics
new_blocks.description_en: The universe is now observed through several messengers — electromagnetic radiation across the spectrum, neutrinos, cosmic rays and gravitational waves — whose combination pinpoints events such as neutron-star mergers and gamma-ray bursts.
new_blocks.description_cs: Vesmír se nyní pozoruje prostřednictvím několika poslů — elektromagnetického záření napříč spektrem, neutrin, kosmického záření a gravitačních vln — jejichž kombinace přesně určuje děje, jako je splývání neutronových hvězd a záblesky gama.

brief_concepts.name: Gamma-ray burst
brief_concepts.definition: The brightest electromagnetic explosion, from collapsing stars or merging compact objects.

brief_concepts.name: Neutrino astronomy
brief_concepts.definition: Observation of astrophysical neutrinos that escape dense sources.

brief_concepts.name: Gravitational-wave astronomy
brief_concepts.definition: The detection of spacetime ripples from merging compact objects.

brief_concepts.name: Kilonova
brief_concepts.definition: The optical glow of a neutron-star merger forging heavy elements.

brief_concepts.name: Messenger coincidence
brief_concepts.definition: The joint detection of one event across multiple channels, localising its source.

new_blocks.name: Seismic Waves & Earthquakes
new_blocks.description_en: Earthquakes radiate elastic seismic waves — fast compressional P-waves, slower shear S-waves, and surface waves — whose travel times and paths are recorded on seismographs and used to locate sources and measure magnitude.
new_blocks.description_cs: Zemětřesení vyzařují elastické seismické vlny — rychlé podélné vlny P, pomalejší příčné vlny S a povrchové vlny — jejichž časy šíření a dráhy zaznamenávají seismografy a používají se k lokalizaci ohnisek a měření magnituda.

brief_concepts.name: P-wave
brief_concepts.definition: The fastest seismic wave, a compressional wave travelling through solids and liquids.

brief_concepts.name: S-wave
brief_concepts.definition: A shear wave travelling only through solids, revealing the liquid outer core by its absence.

brief_concepts.name: Surface waves
brief_concepts.definition: Slower waves confined to the surface that cause most earthquake damage.

brief_concepts.name: Seismograph
brief_concepts.definition: The instrument recording ground motion from seismic waves.

brief_concepts.name: Magnitude
brief_concepts.definition: A logarithmic measure of an earthquake's energy release, such as the moment magnitude.

new_blocks.name: Earth's Internal Structure
new_blocks.description_en: Seismic waves refract and reflect at internal boundaries, revealing the Earth's layers: a thin crust, a solid convecting mantle, a liquid outer core generating the magnetic field, and a solid inner core.
new_blocks.description_cs: Seismické vlny se lámou a odrážejí na vnitřních rozhraních a odhalují vrstvy Země: tenkou kůru, pevný konvektující plášť, tekuté vnější jádro generující magnetické pole a pevné vnitřní jádro.

brief_concepts.name: Crust
brief_concepts.definition: The thin outermost rocky layer, continental or oceanic.

brief_concepts.name: Mantle
brief_concepts.definition: The thick solid layer that convects slowly over geological time.

brief_concepts.name: Outer core
brief_concepts.definition: The liquid iron layer whose motion generates the magnetic field.

brief_concepts.name: Inner core
brief_concepts.definition: The solid iron-nickel centre of the Earth.

brief_concepts.name: Seismic discontinuity
brief_concepts.definition: A depth where wave speed changes abruptly, marking a layer boundary.

new_blocks.name: The Geomagnetic Field & Geodynamo
new_blocks.description_en: The Earth generates a magnetic field by dynamo action in its convecting liquid outer core; the field shields the surface from the solar wind, drifts and weakens over time, and reverses polarity at irregular intervals.
new_blocks.description_cs: Země generuje magnetické pole dynamovým působením ve svém konvektujícím tekutém vnějším jádru; pole chrání povrch před slunečním větrem, s časem se posouvá a slábne a v nepravidelných intervalech přepóluje.

brief_concepts.name: Geodynamo
brief_concepts.definition: The self-sustaining generation of the magnetic field by core convection.

brief_concepts.name: Magnetosphere
brief_concepts.definition: The region of space dominated by the Earth's field, deflecting the solar wind.

brief_concepts.name: Geomagnetic reversal
brief_concepts.definition: The occasional flip of the field's north and south polarity.

brief_concepts.name: Palaeomagnetism
brief_concepts.definition: The record of past field directions frozen into rocks.

brief_concepts.name: Secular variation
brief_concepts.definition: The slow change of the field's strength and direction over decades to centuries.

new_blocks.name: Gravity Field & Geodesy
new_blocks.description_en: Geodesy measures the Earth's shape, orientation and gravity field; departures of gravity from a uniform ellipsoid, the anomalies, map density variations and the isostatic balance of crustal loads on the mantle.
new_blocks.description_cs: Geodézie měří tvar, orientaci a tíhové pole Země; odchylky tíže od rovnoměrného elipsoidu, tíhové anomálie, mapují změny hustoty a izostatickou rovnováhu zatížení kůry na plášti.

brief_concepts.name: Geoid
brief_concepts.definition: The equipotential surface of the gravity field approximating mean sea level.

brief_concepts.name: Reference ellipsoid
brief_concepts.definition: The smooth mathematical figure approximating the Earth's shape.

brief_concepts.name: Gravity anomaly
brief_concepts.definition: The difference between measured and predicted gravity, revealing subsurface density.

brief_concepts.name: Isostasy
brief_concepts.definition: The buoyant equilibrium of crustal blocks floating on the denser mantle.

brief_concepts.name: Satellite geodesy
brief_concepts.definition: The use of satellites to measure the Earth's shape, gravity and rotation.

new_blocks.name: Plate Tectonics
new_blocks.description_en: The Earth's rigid outer shell is broken into plates that move over the ductile mantle, interacting at boundaries where they spread apart, collide or slide past one another, driving earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building.
new_blocks.description_cs: Tuhý vnější obal Země je rozlámán na desky, které se pohybují po tvárném plášti a vzájemně na sebe působí na rozhraních, kde se rozestupují, srážejí nebo se míjejí, čímž pohánějí zemětřesení, vulkanismus a horotvornou činnost.

brief_concepts.name: Lithospheric plate
brief_concepts.definition: A rigid segment of the outer Earth that moves as a unit.

brief_concepts.name: Divergent boundary
brief_concepts.definition: A boundary where plates spread apart and new crust forms.

brief_concepts.name: Convergent boundary
brief_concepts.definition: A boundary where plates collide, forming subduction zones or mountains.

brief_concepts.name: Transform boundary
brief_concepts.definition: A boundary where plates slide horizontally past each other.

brief_concepts.name: Subduction
brief_concepts.definition: The sinking of one plate beneath another into the mantle.

new_blocks.name: Mantle Convection & Earth's Heat
new_blocks.description_en: Heat from the planet's formation and radioactive decay drives slow convection in the solid mantle, the engine of plate motion; measured surface heat flow constrains the planet's thermal history and internal dynamics.
new_blocks.description_cs: Teplo z formování planety a z radioaktivního rozpadu pohání pomalou konvekci v pevném plášti, motor pohybu desek; měřený povrchový tepelný tok omezuje tepelnou historii planety a její vnitřní dynamiku.

brief_concepts.name: Mantle convection
brief_concepts.definition: The slow creeping flow of the solid mantle transporting heat outward.

brief_concepts.name: Radiogenic heat
brief_concepts.definition: Heat produced by the decay of radioactive isotopes in the Earth.

brief_concepts.name: Heat flow
brief_concepts.definition: The rate at which heat escapes through the Earth's surface.

brief_concepts.name: Mantle plume
brief_concepts.definition: An upwelling of hot mantle feeding volcanic hotspots.

brief_concepts.name: Rheology
brief_concepts.definition: The deformation behaviour of rock that lets the solid mantle flow over long times.

new_blocks.name: Protein Structure & Folding
new_blocks.description_en: Proteins fold from linear chains into specific three-dimensional shapes that determine their function, driven toward a free-energy minimum by hydrophobic, electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding forces; misfolding underlies several diseases.
new_blocks.description_cs: Bílkoviny se sbalují z lineárních řetězců do specifických trojrozměrných tvarů určujících jejich funkci, vedeny k minimu volné energie hydrofobními, elektrostatickými a vodíkovými vazbami; chybné sbalení je základem několika onemocnění.

brief_concepts.name: Protein folding
brief_concepts.definition: The process by which a polypeptide chain adopts its functional three-dimensional structure.

brief_concepts.name: Free-energy landscape
brief_concepts.definition: The funnel of conformational energies guiding a protein to its native state.

brief_concepts.name: Hydrophobic effect
brief_concepts.definition: The tendency of nonpolar groups to cluster away from water, driving folding.

brief_concepts.name: Conformational change
brief_concepts.definition: A functional shape change of a protein in response to binding or signals.

brief_concepts.name: Misfolding
brief_concepts.definition: Incorrect folding producing aggregates linked to disease.

new_blocks.name: Molecular Motors & Machines
new_blocks.description_en: Molecular motors convert chemical energy into directed motion and force, walking along filaments or rotating within membranes; they power muscle contraction, intracellular transport and the synthesis of the cell's energy currency.
new_blocks.description_cs: Molekulární motory přeměňují chemickou energii na řízený pohyb a sílu, kráčejí podél filament nebo rotují v membránách; pohánějí svalový stah, nitrobuněčný transport a syntézu energetické měny buňky.

brief_concepts.name: Molecular motor
brief_concepts.definition: A protein converting chemical energy into mechanical work.

brief_concepts.name: ATP hydrolysis
brief_concepts.definition: The energy-releasing reaction powering most molecular motors.

brief_concepts.name: Cytoskeletal transport
brief_concepts.definition: The motor-driven movement of cargo along filaments within cells.

brief_concepts.name: Brownian ratchet
brief_concepts.definition: A mechanism rectifying random thermal motion into directed movement.

brief_concepts.name: Rotary motor
brief_concepts.definition: A membrane machine such as the one synthesising the cell's energy currency by rotation.

new_blocks.name: Membrane Potentials & Ion Transport
new_blocks.description_en: Cell membranes maintain electrical potentials by selectively transporting ions through channels and pumps; the resulting gradients store energy and set the resting potential from which excitable cells generate signals.
new_blocks.description_cs: Buněčné membrány udržují elektrické potenciály selektivním transportem iontů skrze kanály a pumpy; vzniklé gradienty ukládají energii a určují klidový potenciál, z něhož dráždivé buňky vytvářejí signály.

brief_concepts.name: Membrane potential
brief_concepts.definition: The voltage difference across a cell membrane.

brief_concepts.name: Ion channel
brief_concepts.definition: A membrane protein allowing specific ions to flow down their gradient.

brief_concepts.name: Ion pump
brief_concepts.definition: A protein using energy to move ions against their gradient.

brief_concepts.name: Nernst potential
brief_concepts.definition: The equilibrium voltage for an ion set by its concentration ratio.

brief_concepts.name: Resting potential
brief_concepts.definition: The steady membrane voltage of an unstimulated cell.

new_blocks.name: The Action Potential & Nerve Signalling
new_blocks.description_en: Excitable cells fire action potentials — rapid, self-propagating reversals of membrane potential driven by voltage-gated ion channels — which carry electrical signals along nerves, as captured by the Hodgkin-Huxley model.
new_blocks.description_cs: Dráždivé buňky generují akční potenciály — rychlé, samovolně se šířící obrácení membránového potenciálu poháněná napěťově řízenými iontovými kanály — které přenášejí elektrické signály podél nervů, jak popisuje Hodgkinův–Huxleyův model.

brief_concepts.name: Action potential
brief_concepts.definition: A rapid all-or-nothing reversal of membrane potential that propagates along a cell.

brief_concepts.name: Voltage-gated channel
brief_concepts.definition: An ion channel that opens in response to membrane voltage.

brief_concepts.name: Hodgkin-Huxley model
brief_concepts.definition: The quantitative model of the action potential from ionic currents.

brief_concepts.name: Saltatory conduction
brief_concepts.definition: The jumping of nerve impulses between gaps in the myelin sheath, speeding signalling.

brief_concepts.name: Synaptic transmission
brief_concepts.definition: The passing of a signal between cells at a synapse.

new_blocks.name: Tissue Mechanics & Locomotion
new_blocks.description_en: Biomechanics applies the mechanics of materials and forces to living tissue: bones, muscles and tendons carry loads and store elastic energy, and the physics of levers and gaits governs how organisms move.
new_blocks.description_cs: Biomechanika aplikuje mechaniku materiálů a sil na živou tkáň: kosti, svaly a šlachy nesou zatížení a ukládají pružnou energii a fyzika pák a chůze určuje, jak se organismy pohybují.

brief_concepts.name: Tissue elasticity
brief_concepts.definition: The stress-strain response of biological materials such as bone and tendon.

brief_concepts.name: Muscle mechanics
brief_concepts.definition: The force-length and force-velocity behaviour of contracting muscle.

brief_concepts.name: Lever systems
brief_concepts.definition: The skeletal arrangements of bones and muscles acting as levers.

brief_concepts.name: Gait
brief_concepts.definition: The mechanical pattern of legged locomotion optimising energy and stability.

brief_concepts.name: Scaling laws
brief_concepts.definition: How mechanical demands change with organism size.

new_blocks.name: Biological Fluid Dynamics
new_blocks.description_en: The flow of biological fluids follows the physics of hydrodynamics adapted to living systems: blood circulates through branching vessels, air moves through the lungs, and microorganisms swim at low Reynolds number where viscosity dominates.
new_blocks.description_cs: Proudění biologických tekutin se řídí fyzikou hydrodynamiky přizpůsobenou živým systémům: krev obíhá větvícími se cévami, vzduch proudí plícemi a mikroorganismy plavou při nízkém Reynoldsově čísle, kde převládá viskozita.

brief_concepts.name: Haemodynamics
brief_concepts.definition: The physics of blood flow through the circulatory system.

brief_concepts.name: Poiseuille flow
brief_concepts.definition: The pressure-driven laminar flow of fluid through a tube.

brief_concepts.name: Low Reynolds number
brief_concepts.definition: The viscosity-dominated regime in which microorganisms swim.

brief_concepts.name: Respiratory flow
brief_concepts.definition: The mechanics of air movement in breathing.

brief_concepts.name: Wall shear stress
brief_concepts.definition: The frictional force of flowing fluid on vessel walls, sensed by cells.

new_blocks.name: Structural & Single-Molecule Methods
new_blocks.description_en: Physical techniques resolve biological structure and dynamics down to single molecules: X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance yield atomic structures, while optical tweezers and single-molecule fluorescence probe individual molecules at work.
new_blocks.description_cs: Fyzikální techniky rozlišují biologickou strukturu a dynamiku až na úroveň jednotlivých molekul: rentgenová krystalografie, kryoelektronová mikroskopie a nukleární magnetická rezonance dávají atomární struktury, zatímco optická pinzeta a jednomolekulová fluorescence zkoumají jednotlivé molekuly při práci.

brief_concepts.name: X-ray crystallography
brief_concepts.definition: Determining atomic structure from the diffraction of X-rays by a crystal.

brief_concepts.name: Cryo-electron microscopy
brief_concepts.definition: Imaging frozen biomolecules at near-atomic resolution by electron microscopy.

brief_concepts.name: Nuclear magnetic resonance
brief_concepts.definition: Probing molecular structure and dynamics through nuclear spin resonance.

brief_concepts.name: Optical tweezers
brief_concepts.definition: Trapping and manipulating single molecules or particles with focused light.

brief_concepts.name: Single-molecule fluorescence
brief_concepts.definition: Observing individual molecules by the light they emit.

new_blocks.name: Physics of Medical Imaging
new_blocks.description_en: Medical imaging applies physics to see inside the body without surgery: X-ray and computed tomography use ionising radiation, magnetic resonance imaging uses nuclear spins in magnetic fields, and ultrasound uses reflected sound waves.
new_blocks.description_cs: Lékařské zobrazování aplikuje fyziku k pohledu dovnitř těla bez operace: rentgen a výpočetní tomografie využívají ionizující záření, magnetická rezonance využívá jaderné spiny v magnetickém poli a ultrazvuk využívá odražené zvukové vlny.

brief_concepts.name: Computed tomography
brief_concepts.definition: Reconstruction of cross-sectional images from many X-ray projections.

brief_concepts.name: Magnetic resonance imaging
brief_concepts.definition: Imaging based on the nuclear magnetic resonance of tissue protons.

brief_concepts.name: Ultrasound imaging
brief_concepts.definition: Imaging from the echoes of high-frequency sound waves.

brief_concepts.name: Contrast mechanism
brief_concepts.definition: The physical property that distinguishes tissues in an image.

brief_concepts.name: Spatial resolution
brief_concepts.definition: The finest detail an imaging method can resolve.
